title: 國模Agent第一！MiniMax爆改Flash戰力，全時段大肥魚谷價
abstract: 國模Agent第一！MiniMax爆改Flash戰力，全時段大肥魚谷價 Jay 2026-10-20 21:29:54 來源： 量子位 兔皮底下，竟然是MiniMax！ Jay發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號QbitAI 國慶期間在OpenRouter上橫空出世、匿名屠榜的神秘模型 Space Bunny （玉兔），馬甲終於被扒下來了。 兔皮底下，竟然是MiniMax！ 正式交卷的代號是 M3.1 Flash 。 而這個正式版的跑分能力，比Space Bunny還要猛一點，尤其是Agent這個技能點—— Agents’ Last Exam (ALE)得分29.6%，斬獲國模第一。 AA榜單上也是拿到了43分，Flash能有這個成績還是可以。 總之幹活能力終於是上來了，晉升高階牛馬（doge）。 除此之外，Coding、網路安全、Computer Use……也全部殺進全球第一梯隊。 在此基礎上，「玉兔」時期的速度也是依然保持住的，輸出最快可達200+ TPS。 然後，最重要的來了—— 不愧是Flash啊， 這價格是真便宜！！ 輸入每百萬Token 1元，輸出4元，快取讀取只要0.1元。 綜合成本直接壓到了上一代M3的30%。 什麼，你對這個價格還是沒有直觀的印象？？ 這麼說吧—— 和谷期的V4.1 Flash差不多。 太仁義了嗷，我宣佈，以後閒時梁文谷，忙時閆俊峰！（bushi） △ 圖源：@大廠顯微鏡 不過，矽谷閉源陣營恐怕又得遭殃了。 繼DeepSeek之後，矽谷一眾大參數旗艦，又被國產Flash架上了一條全新的價效比斬殺線o(╥﹏╥)o。 文本模型翻身仗 說實話，之前我對MiniMax有過不少嘀咕。 多模態和影片生成確實很頂，但純文本大模型這邊吧，不知道從什麼時候開始就沒動靜了。。。 這次M3.1 Flash亮相，也算是打了場翻身仗吧。 咱們挨個看下戰績： 程式碼工程與真實修Bug 在DeepSWE v1.1評測裡，M3.1 Flash拿下了73.7%。 也是倒反天罡了。 GPT-6.1 Sol、Claude Opus 5、Claude Fable 5……居然被一款Flash跑分反超。 排在它前頭的，只剩下DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017的77分。 這也印證了玉兔匿名測試期間社群的反饋：在處理Three.js這類3D渲染和複雜前端任務時，它對細節的把控極其變態。 網路安全實戰 在加州大學伯克利分校主導的CyberGym基準測試中，M3.1 Flash斬獲82.2分，穩穩跟GLM-5.3（84.5）以及GPT-5.6 Sol（83.6）並排坐在全球第一梯隊。 複雜Agent與企業級跨SaaS工作流 在自動化巨頭Zapier開源的AutomationBench-AA評測中，M3.1 Flash位居前列。 單任務成本不到0.05美元，就能自己串起橫跨銷售、營銷、客服、財務和HR的複雜工作流。 在容錯率極低的金融專屬基準BankerToolBench上，M3.1 Flash更是直接飆到了76.2分，與公認的天花板Claude Opus 5並列全球第一。 Computer Use真實桌面操作 模擬真實電腦操作的OSWorld V2拿到61.7分； 在衡量真實並有經濟價值場景的ALE上，M3.1 Flash也以極低的任務成本，實現了頂尖模型級別的效能表現。 兩項均位列國產模型第一，又是一個斬殺一切的價效比大法。 說真的，我想過MiniMax的文本模型遲早會重回牌桌。 但誰能想到，是一個帶Flash字尾的小傢伙。。。 極速低價才是王道 只看基準跑分，你可能還覺得這只是神仙打架的日常。 真正讓人興奮的，是這個模型對實際落地場景的降維打擊。 大家平時搭多Agent協同或者長鏈路工作流，最怕遇到什麼？ 兩件事： 無休止的轉圈等待，以及月底讓人心驚肉跳的API賬單。 一個真正的企業級Agent，在後臺往往要調幾十次工具、在好幾個子Agent之間反覆傳話。 模型吐字慢，使用者看著介面轉圈直接關掉網頁；呼叫單價貴，財務看一眼賬單當場就能把專案叫停。 M3.1 Flash爽就爽在這裡。 它底層上了相當 激進的稀疏注意力架構 。 線上推理速度直接拉昇將近3倍，輸出速度最快可達200+ TPS，中位數（P50）也穩穩維持在170+TPS。 170 TPS是什麼概念？ 你在MiniMax Code桌面端、Claude Code或者各種本地Coding工具裡派發一個重構任務，螢幕上的程式碼幾乎是以傾瀉的狀態瞬間刷滿。 以前串聯四個子Agent像是在等紅綠燈，現在幾乎做到了無感重新整理。 速度起飛的同時， 價格更是直接打骨折 ： 輸入價格：每百萬Token只要1元 輸出價格：每百萬Token只要4元 快取讀取價格：每百萬Token只要0.1元 輸入和輸出價格直接腰斬，快取讀取費用更是直降75%。 結果就是，綜合使用成本相比前代M3暴降70%。 那還說啥了， 站起來蹬吧家人們！！ 國產雙子星反圍剿 過去大家有個預設共識：Flash模型無非就是旗艦大模型的廉價閹割版。 選Flash是因為囊中羞澀或者任務太水，真到了關鍵、複雜的硬核場景，最後還得加錢上大參數旗艦Pro。 但現在呢？ DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017前腳剛立下價效比標杆，MiniMax M3.1 Flash後腳就緊跟殺到，一個斬完另一個接著斬。 小尺寸模型根本不是玩具，完全可以正面PK數倍參數、十倍價格的旗艦模型。 黑子，說話！！ 更有意思的是，這兩個國產Flash模型，走出了極其漂亮的互補路線： DeepSeek在純Coding的極致價效比上拔得頭籌； MiniMax M3.1 Flash則在跨SaaS企業工作流、金融工具鏈呼叫等綜合Agent維度上有所強化。 一個死磕程式碼工程，一個深耕複雜業務流。 而且家人們，我擱網際網路上一刷，發現了一個天才的idea！ 大肥魚不是有谷價和峰價嗎，但之前苦於一直沒有同等級價效比模型，峰價咬咬牙也吃了。 但現在M3.1一出來，正好補上位了啊。 我直接一個路由， 忙時MiniMax，閒時大肥魚 ，徹底將Token紅利吃幹抹淨。 淚目了，這就是咱激動人心的國產Flash組合技（bushi）。 這樣一來，我覺得， API其實也是普通使用者可以考慮一下的選擇了 。 畢竟大模型這玩意兒嘛，迭代實在有點太快了，就算買的只是包月。 你像Opus 5.5一發，Astra那一波的訂閱使用者，也是基本翻車了。 白買Pro 10X，我好心疼我的錢包。 而且現在C端使用者真的很慘啊o(╥﹏╥)o。 又是5小時限額，又是半夜Reset背刺，動不動還要提防後臺的降智偷襲。。。 買API，充個幾十塊錢，哪個拉胯了隨時拜拜，簡直不要太舒服。 淚目了家人們。 不知道大家有沒有相同感受，說實話，這一個月來我是有點憋屈得慌的。 A社、OpenAI、谷歌瘋狂釋出旗艦模型，反觀國產陣營這邊，啥動靜也沒有啊。 不少大佬也在說，LLM這一戰基本結束了，矽谷靠Scaling殺死了一切。 但如今，拐點，似乎正在出現。 短短兩天，兩款國產Flash模型接連登場。 旗艦級的能力，正在以Flash的速度和價格加速普惠。 確實，SOTA這場仗，不是那麼好打的。 但當「價效比」這一前提得到滿足，另一場更重要的仗—— 大模型產業落地，或許，才剛剛開始。 而這，一直是中國公司，最擅長做的事。 — 完 — 量子位 QbitAI · 頭條號簽約 關注我們，第一時間獲知前沿科技動態 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 MiniMax Jay 谷歌開源RSI新成果！華人濃度爆表 2026-10-19 有預言家！A社研究藍圖曝光，Claude Code來自5年前 2026-10-15 title: RSI三塊關鍵拼圖，MemT 1.0從模型層補上「記憶」
abstract: RSI三塊關鍵拼圖，MemT 1.0從模型層補上「記憶」 鷺羽 2026-10-20 20:50:34 來源： 量子位 把記憶原生焊進Transformer 鷺羽 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI AI圈，最近集體盯上了三個字母： RSI 。 Hinton的RSI論文 ，22位署名作者裡，坐著Bengio、OpenAI首席科學家Pachocki、Anthropic聯創Jack Clark……幾乎AI的半壁江山都在這兒。 大家在將目光投向AI自我改進的同時，一個更值得追問的基礎問題浮出水面： 一次改進，如何成為下一次的起點？ 有效的方法需要被保留，走過的彎路也需要被識別，承接這件事的，其實是 記憶 。 常規的思路很簡單：給AI直接外接一個經驗庫，操作方法、歷史教訓就能通通被儲存檢索。 記憶張量 在這方面的探索，則給出了一份截然不同的答卷——記憶原生。 何為記憶原生？就是將經驗的保留、更新和呼叫，做成模型可以學習的能力。 當記憶在模型中生根發芽，便構成了 記憶原生模型 。 其最新開源釋出的 MemT 1.0 系列，就給出了一條頗為具體的路徑： 它把經驗編碼成內部動態狀態，再通過訓練學習怎樣寫入、更新和讀取，最後讓這些狀態經由記憶分支參與後續計算。 與外部記憶相比，它不僅能力沒打折，未來拓展的天花板也會更高。 這也是記憶原生模型 首次 實現近300B參數規模的工程驗證。 （論文地址指路： https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26825） 好傢伙，記憶看不見摸不著，但卻實打實成為模型成長的立足根本。 從早期要求模型記住資訊，到用好經驗，模型對記憶的要求不斷升級，也讓記憶一步步從幕後走到臺前。 把記憶放進模型 MemT 1.0這次直接甩出兩個型號： MemT-1.0-Nano 總計36B參數、啟用3B，基座用的是“源神”Qwen3.6-35B-A3B； MemT-1.0-Flash 則向上突破，高達288B參數、啟用17B，基座是經過進一步後訓練的DeepSeek-V4-Flash。 它們共同的變化，即都是在選定的Transformer模組裡增加了一條與原有注意力 並行的記憶計算通路 。 咱們舉個簡單的例子說明。 比如同樣面對一個新任務， 外部記憶 的做法是把記憶原文、檢索證據乃至抽象方法塞回上下文，讓模型複用經驗。 其中檢索與整理過程，同樣可以引入學習機制。 而MemT 1.0這類 記憶原生模型 ，選擇繼續深入模型內部： 經驗經過編碼，成為可更新的矩陣狀態；模型生成答案或動作時，通過專門的記憶分支讀取狀態，讀出結果再與原有注意力輸出融合，影響後續生成。 區別落在了經驗如何表示，以及它通過什麼計算過程發揮作用。 但這樣做的好處也很明顯，讓讀寫參與訓練能夠換來更順暢的方法複用，不過代價也有，如果想要精確刪除、解釋與恢復，就需要額外機制的加入。 外部文本肯定更方便檢查和溯源，二者目前來看各有各的優劣。 要說真能看出差別，還得是在用了經驗之後，觀察模型跑起來如何。 先看一個碼農熟悉的場景： 改程式碼 。 接Bug→定位程式碼→動手修改，基本都是這麼個流程。但要是一開始問題沒復現、邊界條件也沒確認好，修改不成反倒漏洞百出，一代傳一代。 拿 SWE-bench Verified 為例，裡面有一項涉及Django的parse_http_date函式，需要修復兩位數年份的解析邏輯。 研究團隊比較了無經驗、文本經驗和記憶原生三種設定下的執行軌跡。 沒有經驗時，Agent找到Bug後，很快開始修改解析邏輯，後續步驟中才出現定向復現與驗證。有經驗的兩組，則都先構建復現測試，再修改程式碼。 其中，MemT-1.0-Nano還在初次修改後 重新檢查了一項邊界條件 ，修正實現，並做了額外驗證。 可以明顯看出，經驗改變了行動順序，也參與了任務內的檢查與修正。 放到更大樣本上對比，在500項SWE-bench Verified任務，每項獨立執行三次中，MemT-1.0-Nano在關鍵斷點的平均成功率為 69.73％ ，無經驗基線為66.07％，文本經驗組為69.13％。 三次全部成功的任務比例，則從無經驗時的54.00％提高到 62.80％ ，文本經驗組為61.80％。 再看 SWE-bench Multilingual 任務中，同一觸發設定下，原生記憶組平均成功率為 63.56％ ，無經驗組為60.00％，文本經驗組為63.00％。 換句話說，這些程式性經驗能通過記憶原生得以保留，表現和顯式文本經驗接近，優勢更多體現在 平均成功率 和重複執行的 可靠性 上。 再直觀一點，來看一段畫素風的 迷宮探索演示 。 同一個迷宮，同樣的移動速度，左邊是沒有記憶原生的Agent，右邊是具備記憶原生的MemT 1.0。 第一輪 ，兩邊都需要探索未知路線，也 都會走進死胡同 。 區別出現在這一輪結束之後：成功路線和需要避開的岔路被整理歸檔，並載入到MemT 1.0的記憶中，為下一輪探索提供參考。 到了 第二輪 ，同樣從起點出發，左邊仍會在岔路上重複試探，右邊則藉助上一輪經驗， 避開已經走過的死胡同 ，沿有效路線抵達終點。 影片連結：https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/DTdaGUk8o0dwkx1wxnnbYw 上一輪走出來的路，開始直接影響下一輪怎麼走，這就是記憶原生值得做的具體體現。 再來一個更接近我們日常辦公的 資訊更新場景 。 展覽原定週六下午3點，後來正式改到週日下午4點。之後又有人建議改到週一，但還沒確定拍板。 這種反覆變化的資訊增量，其實對AI來說很頭痛。 要記住最後出現的日期還不夠，它還得分清正式決定和隨口建議，以及保留那些沒變的內容。 實驗在經過多輪對話後，MemT-1.0-Nano仍然 成功get ，回答出了原定時間、正式修改後的時間，並確認其他安排沒有變化。 放進11項記憶基準的綜合評估中，Flash和Nano的表現也同樣突出。 平均得分分別為50.6和47.0，位列參與評估的參數化記憶方法 前兩名 ，相比其它模型斷崖式領先。 不過坦白來說，文本記憶系統整體仍有優勢，尤其是在長歷史的細節召回上。 MemT 1.0今天交出的，還只是記憶原生新思路的初步計算實現，但實際效果已經能和文本記憶比肩，再繼續發展下去，潛力亦是無限。 記憶原生，原生在哪裡？ 那麼問題來了，經驗沒有留在任務上下文裡，模型又是從哪裡把它用上的？ 這恰是MemT 1.0的 架構 重點。 MemT 1.0提供的原生路徑，是先將 相關經驗編碼 為內部動態狀態。生成後續動作時，當前查詢通過 專門的記憶分支讀取 該狀態，再將結果與原有注意力輸出融合。 在具體參數化實現中，MemT 1.0保留基座的原有計算流程，在選定的Transformer模組中加入原生記憶分支，拆開看包括三層： 主幹權重：承載模型已有的通用能力，並在訓練記憶時保持凍結； 超記憶：讀寫投影、門控這類可訓練參數決定具體怎樣編碼、更新和讀取記憶； 局部記憶：動態矩陣狀態儲存互動中新加入的資訊。 這樣區分後，模型不僅能帶上新的經歷，也不必每次都去微調整個主幹，只有對應任務軌跡的動態狀態發生變化。 這套機制的讀寫也很有講究。 寫入時，隱狀態經過投影，生成記憶的鍵值；擦除、寫入和遺忘門控，共同調節已有矩陣中的關聯；讀取時，當前輸入被對映為記憶查詢，讀出相關資訊，再經歸一化和輸出門控參與後續生成。 更新機制採用的是基於 Gated DeltaNet-2 的逐Token生成，並做了穩定化處理。 （小道訊息：Gated DeltaNet-2的作者也參與了相關討論） 它會在每一輪結束後觸發，靠門控調整已有記憶關聯，輪內則仍按Token順序調整狀態。 消融實驗證明了這一點，將逐Token更新換成整輪聚合後，Nano的記憶基準平均分從約47.0降到了41.0。 六分的差距 ，足以說明連續的Token級更新能更好地處理記憶衰減，並及時修正輪內關聯。 但當記憶的內容不斷擴充，模型容量不夠了怎麼辦？ 這時MemT 1.0又依託MoE，提出了 MoS （Mixture-of-Storage）解決方案。 MoS將一個記憶原生模組擴展為多個記憶專家，再分別學習儲存與使用路由。其採用的是 稠密融合 ，所有記憶專家都參與計算，路由權重決定各自貢獻。 這就與基座MoE的稀疏專家路由明顯不同了。 不過，結構還只是起點。 為了讓模型真正學會使用這條通路，團隊構建了340億Token的記憶訓練語料，其中包含繼續預訓練200億，後訓練140億。 繼續預訓練 的格式都是統一的，先把長文本切成連續片段寫進記憶，再讓模型拿著記憶狀態去回答查詢。 每處理完一個片段，模型再更新狀態，供下一段使用。 後訓練 進一步對齊任務結果，資料也包含三類：記憶原生的 語言建模資料 、 記憶儲存與利用資料 （比如摘要、續寫、壓縮等），以及專門強化長程記憶的 任務資料 。 這裡也有一點值得單獨拎出來講， 此前凍結的主幹會充當教師模型 ，看到完整的歷史資訊， MemT 1.0作為學生 ，只能看到自己的記憶狀態，再沿著off-policy蒸餾讓學生去對齊教師的分佈。 綜合下來，記憶原生的重點逐漸清晰，把歷史編碼成狀態還只是第一步，接著怎樣保留、更新和讀取才構成記憶原生模型的全部。 這條路線的價值，還需要結合經驗複用效果、資源開銷和長期執行條件來綜合判斷。 從持續學習到RSI，記憶開啟能力增長空間 那麼又有朋友可能要問了， 為什麼要用記憶原生？ 現有的外部記憶方案已經很成熟了，也有不錯的實踐案例，相比之下，記憶原生才剛起步，效果也大差不差。 非也！記憶原生也有個獨到之處： 它讓經驗的表示與讀寫本身，開始成為模型能力擴展的物件，也就是MemT團隊討論的Memory Scaling，即從推理增長之外，找到模型效能增長的第三條曲線。 圖片由AI生成 原來的經驗有沒有用，可以看檢索後能否改善任務結果；到了MemT 1.0這裡，還可以進一步追問：同樣的經歷，換一種內部表示、更新規則和讀取方式，能不能用得更好？ 這讓提升記憶效果多了 一組可以通過訓練和架構設計調整的變數 。 誠然，這還遠不能證明原生記憶的長期上限高於外部記憶，但至少圍繞內部狀態的訓練與容量擴展，可以帶來進一步的 能力收益 。 下一步是驗證這些收益能否跨出當前訓練分佈，在更長互動和新任務中保持。 回到開頭的RSI。 一旦打通了記憶原生，對 持續學習和RSI 的突破也是大有裨益。 眾所周知，RSI有三塊拼圖，包括 記憶、反饋、驗證與更新機制 ，其中記憶讓有效結果能夠延續，後兩者幫助判斷哪些改變值得進入下一輪。 MemT 1.0如今探索的，正是經驗承接與複用這一步，它驗證了經驗能通過原生記憶指導行動， 從模型層面補上了第一塊 ，當然也是最重要的一塊。 圖片由AI生成 如果再往前走，也許局部記憶中積累的經驗，就能通過後續訓練沉澱到超記憶參數，再反過來改善模型管理記憶的方法。 一旦這個環節成立，通過記錄下來的結果和方法，系統或許可以實現跨任務的智慧爆炸，也就是RSI的終極目標。 這些還只是理論層面的收益，在應用側，記憶原生也 更有利於企業完成經驗積累 。 當前行業一說到企業AI，考慮最多的還是 早期部署階段 的內容，比如當前模型好不好用、能做到哪一步。 這固然沒毛病，但企業用起來後，才知道經驗積累也很重要。 因為企業長期使用還涉及專案規則、操作順序和驗證方法。如果每換一項任務，都得重新交代同類約束、重複經歷同類失敗，前一次投入就很難充分轉化為後續收益。 所以對於這類重複的工作流， 經過驗證的經驗能複用多少次 ，應該和 模型單次表現 一起進入企業AI選型標準。 記憶原生為此提供了 模型側 的承載機制。 在同樣的128K長歷史下，Nano的端到端推理速度約為完整上下文方案的1.86倍，相同歷史長度中，每條軌跡的持久狀態佔用是完整上下文KV Cache的六十六分之一。 翻譯一下，這就是立竿見影的 成本控制效果 。 長期會話的狀態預算更容易被估算，多個查詢還可以複用已構建的狀態，分攤準備開銷。 不過這裡也要說句公道話，並不是記憶原生的任務質量一定優於外部記憶，但在近似質量的情形裡，它更有可能通過底層的經驗複用穩步減少返工，這部分收益對 企業運維 來說卻是實實在在的。 換言之，記憶原生和外部記憶並不是非此即彼的敵對關係，二者協作分工，或許能產生更大的額外收益。 對精確原文、來源或版本的查詢，外部記錄仍有價值；針對後續執行的經驗呼叫，可以繼續檢驗原生機制的作用。 但無論如何，當有效進步能夠留下，並在新任務中反覆經受驗證， 持續自我改進才有了可以積累的起點。 通過完整的分層記憶管理和排程，即可實現全域性的讀寫效率最優，而今天，記憶原生模型的釋出，已讓這種 工程化部署和實現 成為了可能。 記憶在推動持續自我改進方面的價值，也將在這樣的長期驗證中逐漸顯現。 GitHub連結： https://github.com/MemTensor/MemT-1.0 title: 比亞迪成為2026年APEC會議官方合作夥伴
abstract: 比亞迪成為2026年APEC會議官方合作夥伴 量子位的朋友們 2026-10-20 17:57:35 來源： 量子位 2026年10月16日，比亞迪集團正式成為亞太經合組織第三十三次領導人非正式會議官方合作夥伴 2026年10月16日，比亞迪集團正式成為亞太經合組織第三十三次領導人非正式會議官方合作夥伴（簡稱：2026年APEC會議官方合作夥伴），旗下騰勢汽車、仰望汽車、方程豹汽車、比亞迪汽車王朝和海洋的多款高階車型成為2026年APEC會議官方指定用車，將為參會嘉賓提供綠色出行保障，助力APEC會議落實低碳辦會要求，展示中國新能源汽車產業的創新成果，彰顯中國智造風采。 作為紮根深圳，全球最大的新能源汽車企業，比亞迪始終堅持“技術為王，創新為本”的發展理念，相繼推出了第二代刀片電池及閃充技術、“天神之眼”智慧輔助駕駛系統、雲輦、易四方等多項顛覆性創新技術，持續引領全球新能源汽車變革。2025年比亞迪新能源汽車銷量超460萬輛，蟬聯全球銷冠，海外銷量突破104萬輛，同比增長145%；2026年1-9月累計銷量超313萬輛，海外累計銷售超133萬輛。如今，比亞迪新能源汽車足跡遍及全球120多個國家和地區，以技術創新助力全球碳中和，為世界綠色出行貢獻中國方案。 本文由比亞迪提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 比亞迪 量子位的朋友們 2026物理AI與世界模型大會醫療健康世界模型分會場在南京舉行 2026-10-19 技術賦能全球化深耕 比亞迪攜多品牌亮相2026巴黎車展 2026-10-20 Meshy推出Meshy Edit：基於全新自研AI模型，一句指令實現3D模型局部編輯 2026-10-20 AI硬體出海，別當“背景板”，GTC2026 Shanghai「AI硬體專區」邀你佔位 2026-10-20 相關閱讀

title: 技術賦能全球化深耕 比亞迪攜多品牌亮相2026巴黎車展
abstract: 技術賦能全球化深耕 比亞迪攜多品牌亮相2026巴黎車展 量子位的朋友們 2026-10-20 17:13:14 來源： 量子位 當地時間10月12日，2026巴黎國際車展正式啟幕。 當地時間10月12日，2026巴黎國際車展正式啟幕。比亞迪集團閃充旗艦登陸歐洲，攜比亞迪、騰勢雙品牌重磅登場，集中展示全系新能源產品矩陣、第二代刀片電池及閃充技術、“天神之眼”智慧輔助駕駛等前沿核心技術，全面展現企業持續深耕歐洲市場、以技術創新驅動全球化高質量發展的戰略實力與堅定信心。 本屆巴黎車展，比亞迪帶來多款面向歐洲市場的戰略新品與技術成果，實現純電、超級混動、輔助智慧駕駛、極速補能全維度技術落地，進一步完善在歐產品佈局與技術生態。其中，比亞迪ATTO 8作為品牌登陸歐洲的首款搭載第二代刀片電池車型正式亮相，憑藉更強安全效能、更高能量密度與極速閃充能力，為歐洲家庭使用者帶來高階純電出行新選擇。 高階品牌騰勢同步帶來重磅產品與前瞻規劃，展出超級混動越野車型BAO 5、旗艦超跑騰勢Z系列等重磅產品，並正式官宣城市領航輔助駕駛（CNOA）將於2027年率先落地歐洲市場、搭載於騰勢Z9GT，標誌著比亞迪高階智慧駕駛技術全面開啟歐洲市場化程序，進一步提升海外高階智慧化出行體驗。 在本地化產品佈局上，比亞迪持續立足歐洲使用者需求實現定向研發、專屬打造。本次展出的DOLPHIN G DM-i是比亞迪專為歐洲市場開發的緊湊型超級混動車型，將高效節能的DM-i超級混動技術引入歐洲主流家用車細分市場，填補區域市場技術空白。全新推出的BYD SHARK超級混動皮卡，則將DMO超級混動越野平臺優勢延伸至全新細分賽道，助力比亞迪在歐洲構建家用、越野、皮卡全覆蓋的多元化產品矩陣。 依託全產業鏈自主研發與垂直整合優勢，比亞迪在本屆車展集中展示核心技術底座，涵蓋第二代刀片電池及閃充技術、純電專屬平臺、DM-i超級混動、DMO超級混動越野平臺等自研技術體系，充分彰顯企業覆蓋整車製造、核心零部件研發、能源解決方案的全鏈條綜合實力。補能生態層面，比亞迪明確2027年底前在歐洲建成3000座閃充站的基礎設施規劃，通過產品、技術、補能網路三位一體協同落地，持續破解海外使用者補能痛點，構建高效、便捷、完善的本地化新能源出行生態。 比亞迪執行副總裁李柯表示，閃充技術可實現媲美燃油車的補能效率，有效緩解使用者里程與補能焦慮。與此同時，“天神之眼”高階智慧駕駛系統，可高效應對歐洲城市複雜路況，大幅提升駕駛安全性與便捷度。依託閃充技術、易三方平臺、高階智駕等前沿創新成果，比亞迪和騰勢持續將領先技術優勢轉化為使用者價值，讓全球消費者共享新能源技術發展紅利。 全球化佈局持續提速，市場認可度穩步攀升。截至2026年9月，比亞迪新能源汽車業務已覆蓋全球120多個國家和地區，全球累計銷量突破1820萬輛。2026年前九個月，比亞迪乘用車及皮卡海外銷量突破133萬輛，已超越2025全年海外銷量，海外市場增長勢能持續釋放，充分印證全球市場對比亞迪技術、產品與品質的高度認可。 面向未來，比亞迪將持續以技術創新為核心驅動力，依託多品牌、多技術、全品類產品矩陣，精準匹配全球不同區域市場需求。同時持續完善海外技術落地、產品迭代、補能網路與服務體系建設，加速推動全球綠色智慧出行普及，為全球汽車產業高質量發展持續貢獻中國力量。 本文由比亞迪提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 比亞迪 量子位的朋友們 飛書豆包工作AI先鋒未來人才大賽：企業正在爭搶會用AI做成事的人 2026-10-21 比亞迪成為2026年APEC會議官方合作夥伴 2026-10-20 2026物理AI與世界模型大會醫療健康世界模型分會場在南京舉行 2026-10-19 Meshy推出Meshy Edit：基於全新自研AI模型，一句指令實現3D模型局部編輯 2026-10-20 相關閱讀

title: 首Token延遲降低32.4%！是石科技叢集排程大招，國產推理再提效
abstract: 首Token延遲降低32.4%！是石科技叢集排程大招，國產推理再提效 思邈 2026-10-20 16:01:25 來源： 量子位 最新發布TokenFleet排程框架 允中 發自 凹非寺量子位 | 公眾號QbitAI GPU集群裡，請求排隊和資源閒置，可能同時發生。 2026 CCF全國高效能運算學術大會期間，是石科技釋出新品 TokenFleet分散式排程框架 ，把最佳化重點放在請求路由、跨機房容量協同和混合負載治理上，嘗試提高現有算力的有效產出。 如果把推理服務看作一座“國產Token優化工廠”，GPU是生產裝置，推理例項是工位，業務請求則是一張張訂單。TokenFleet負責的，就是把訂單與產能匹配起來。 同一批裝置，接到的任務不同、分配方式不同，最終的等待時間與達標產出也會不同。規模化服務，需要把這些生產安排一起考慮。 TokenFleet聚焦叢集的有效產出 模型部署完成之後，叢集還需要同時應對多種業務。 多個模型共享算力，不同租戶有各自的服務等級要求。短對話要及時響應，長文件處理需要更多計算與視訊記憶體，離線批次任務又有完成期限。服務分佈在多個機房時，還要考慮各處的容量能否協同。 簡單分流可能讓部分例項排起長隊，其他位置的容量卻沒有被及時利用。長請求與批次任務相互擠壓，會拖慢即時互動；超時、取消和重複計算，又會消耗資源卻未形成合格交付。 TokenFleet在模型質量、服務要求與算力預算一致的條件下，通過 提高有效Token產出，降低單位有效產出的成本 。 TokenPilot在同一模型池內選擇例項，FleetMind面向跨機房容量協同，SLOMax負責混合負載的准入、佇列治理與容量分配，三項核心技術各有分工。 請求分給誰、任務何時進入佇列、機房容量如何協同，最終都要回到同一個指標：成功完成且滿足服務要求的有效Token產出。 △圖1 TokenFleet三項核心排程技術總覽 TokenPilot把快取收益與排隊代價一起算 先看請求選點。一次請求，應該發給哪個例項？ 一句短問答和一份長文件，即使都算一次請求，消耗的計算與視訊記憶體也可能相差很大。只按請求數量分流，很難均衡各個例項的實際工作量。 快取讓這件事多了一層取捨。帶著相同長字首的請求，如果送到保留了相關KV快取的例項，就有機會複用此前的計算結果，減少Prefill，也就是處理輸入內容時的重複計算。 但快取命中高的例項，也可能排隊久。請求都湧向同一處，省下的計算時間就可能消耗在等待上。 TokenPilot在選點時， 同時估算快取複用收益與排隊代價 。它結合輸入規模、輸出預算和可複用字首估計工作量，再綜合佇列、在途Token、KV快取壓力與預測延遲，篩選並評分候選例項。輸出預算是約束條件，並不代表實際輸出長度。 排程器據此比較不同例項的預計處理代價，判斷複用快取省下的計算，能否抵消額外等待。 △圖2 TokenPilot智慧推理路由框架 是石科技提供的GLM5.3調優資料顯示，在所測顯示卡叢集與負載條件下，採用預測延遲路由後， P95首Token延遲降低32.4%，P50首Token延遲降低71.3% 。 △表1 TokenPilot首Token延遲調優結果。資料來源：是石科技大會演講材料。改善率按（基線值－最佳化值）÷基線值計算；延遲下降不直接等於成本下降。 P50反映中位水平，P95反映尾部請求的等待情況。這組資料展示的是所測條件下的響應改善；成本收益仍需結合吞吐與資源佔用評估。 FleetMind跨機房也要算清服務容量 把視角從一個模型池拉到多個機房，排程就多了一層容量判斷。 有空閒GPU，未必能馬上接單。目標模型是否部署、版本是否匹配、服務端點是否就緒，以及網路傳輸要花多少時間，都會影響分流效果。 FleetMind關注的是 實際可用的模型服務容量 。在TokenFleet的設計中，它匯聚各機房的模型可用性、即時容量與網路狀態，先選擇執行機房，再由該機房的本地決策引擎選擇具體推理例項。 當熱點機房開始排隊，系統會評估其他機房是否有同版本模型的就緒端點、是否仍有服務餘量，再判斷能否承接允許跨地域執行的新請求。 能不能分流，要先滿足許可權和資料地域約束。值不值得分流，還要綜合比較回源時延、排隊、計算、快取與傳輸成本。 容量協同也有不同的時間尺度：短週期調整新請求的去向，長週期調整模型副本與預熱位置，並結合容量預留、負載上限感知和自動回退，減少容量錯配。 △圖3 FleetMind跨機房執行框架。說明：A地為業務入口，不計入GPU容量池；B地為現有叢集，C、D地為擴展機房。 TokenPilot與SLOMax面向現有叢集，FleetMind面向後續新增算力機房的擴展。跨機房協同的目標，是讓符合業務約束的分散容量承接熱點需求，減少容量錯配和重複預留。 SLOMax按服務要求安排生產 請求進入同一個叢集，交付要求卻各不相同。 即時對話關心首Token響應和持續生成速度，長上下文任務更依賴輸入處理能力與KV容量，離線批次任務則關注完成期限和吞吐。把它們放進同一套佇列，容易產生資源爭搶。 長Prefill、KV容量壓力和批次負載，都可能擠壓互動請求。超時、取消與重複執行，還會讓一部分計算無法轉化為有效交付。 SLOMax結合輸入長度、輸出預算、任務型別與租戶服務目標識別工作量，再按等級准入、分池排隊並協調容量。它需要保障互動容量，控制長短請求的併發與相互干擾。 △圖4 SLOMax分類佇列與容量反饋框架。說明：效果反饋用於調整容量與准入，框架不預設執行中任務搶佔能力。 衡量這套排程效果，TokenFleet把達標產出作為最佳化目標。 Goodput，即達標輸出吞吐 ，計算的是：完整測試時段內，成功完成且滿足約定服務要求的請求所產生的輸出Token總量，除以測試時長。不同任務類別需要分別定義達標門檻並報告結果。 系統將達標吞吐、失敗、取消與重複執行情況反饋給排程策略，持續調整准入和容量比例。GPU有多忙、總吞吐有多高，都需要與最終的合格交付一起看。 在是石科技給出的GLM5.3收益測算示例中，採用流控協同排程後，總輸出吞吐增加約1.5%， 達標輸出吞吐提高約29.4% ，達標比例從約67%升至約86%。 △表2 SLOMax有效Token吞吐收益測算示例。資料來源：是石科技大會演講材料。本表為收益測算示例；達標比例沿用原文取整值，變化約19個百分點。 這組數值屬於收益測算，展示了排程希望改善的產出結構。實際收益仍需結合具體負載與服務門檻驗證。 同樣規模的總產出，如果能減少超時、取消和重複計算，就有機會交付更多達標Token。SLOMax把這些結果納入反饋，用於調整後續資源分配。 國產Token優化工廠的效率，還要看排程 TokenFleet把推理服務的最佳化推進到叢集層面。例項效能如何分配給不同請求，多個機房的容量如何參與服務，都需要排程把資源與業務要求接起來。 是石科技（METASTONE）是一家 獨立第三方全棧算力運營商 ，不綁定任何特定大模型廠商，為客戶提供涵蓋 硬體、組網、排程、最佳化與運營的一站式全棧算力交付服務 。 憑藉源自國家級計算中心的豐富經驗，其算力叢集執行SLA達到99.95%以上。目前，是石科技已納管超過20000P+的算力資源，運營10多個超智算中心，其中有2個國家級超算中心；團隊成員曾榮獲3項戈登·貝爾獎，積累了超大規模叢集的全棧技術服務經驗。 圍繞國產Token優化工廠，是石科技以自研自用持續打磨軟體能力，希望讓通用、高頻的推理服務更經濟，讓國產算力發揮更多能力。 此前釋出的Meta-Infer高效推理引擎，著力提升單個推理例項的執行效率。此次TokenFleet則把重點放在 叢集排程 ，通過請求分配、容量協同與混合負載治理，組織規模化服務。 讓更多業務用得起、用得好Token，既需要硬體提供算力，也需要軟體把產能組織起來。 TokenFleet把進一步最佳化的方向，落在了每一次請求如何被分配、每一份容量如何被使用上。 *本文系量子位獲授權刊載，觀點僅為原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 token 推理 是石科技 思邈 量智齊飛！4個月9款車落地，輕舟城市NOA擊穿10-20萬體驗天花板 2026-10-21 通研院孵化的團隊，也盯上了RSI 2026-10-19 title: Meshy推出Meshy Edit：基於全新自研AI模型，一句指令實現3D模型局部編輯
abstract: Meshy推出Meshy Edit：基於全新自研AI模型，一句指令實現3D模型局部編輯 量子位的朋友們 2026-10-20 12:59:04 來源： 量子位 圈選修改區域，一句話描述改動，約一分鐘生成新模型，未選中區域保持原樣 AI 3D 多模態模型公司 Meshy 今日正式釋出局部編輯功能 Meshy Edit。該功能基於 Meshy 全新自研的 AI 模型，使用者只需在 3D 模型上圈出想修改的區域，再用一句話描述改動，約一分鐘即可生成新模型，未選中的區域保持原樣。目前，Meshy Edit 已向全部註冊使用者開放。 模型生成後，創作者往往還需要調整局部，例如移除一件配飾、補充一處細節，或嘗試新的造型。過去，這類修改通常只能通過兩種方式完成：一是重新生成整個模型，但原本想保留的部分也會一併改變；二是藉助 Blender 等專業軟體手動編輯，而這需要長期積累的建模技能。 Meshy Edit 將修改流程簡化為兩步：先選區，再描述。選區時，使用者可以用套索工具圈出整塊部件，選區會同時覆蓋模型的正面、側面和背面；也可以用畫筆塗抹可見表面，對選區邊緣進行微調。完成選區後，使用者用一句話描述改動，比如“去掉帽子”，還可以附上最多 5 張參考圖，輔助說明修改意圖。 每次修改都會生成一個新模型，原模型完整保留。新模型可以繼續編輯、下載，也可以直接傳送到切片軟體，進入 3D 列印流程。 Meshy Edit 主要面向兩類使用者。對於從事手辦、戰棋、潮玩和文創的 3D 列印使用者，該功能支援刪減或新增部件、替換配件，修改完成後即可直接列印。對於遊戲開發者和角色創作者，角色定稿後，只需更換一件道具或配飾，即可在角色本體不變的情況下快速產出多個版本。 Meshy 在個人使用者中的付費表現，也獲得了第三方資料的印證。10 月 5 日，知名風投機構 a16z 釋出第七期《Top 100 生成式 AI 消費級應用》報告，首次增設按月收入排名的 Top 50 榜單。該榜單基於 YipitData 追蹤的美國消費者銀行卡消費資料，因此能直接反映使用者的實際付費情況。Meshy 位列第 31 名，與 Midjourney、Suno、Runway 等創意工具同榜，也是榜單上唯一的 AI 3D 公司。 對付費使用者而言，時間是最直接的成本。在 Blender 中手動修改一處細節可能需要數小時，而使用 Meshy Edit 僅需約一分鐘。滿意的部分原樣保留，創作者可以將精力集中在真正關注的細節上。 價格與可用性 Meshy Edit 現已向全部註冊使用者開放，每次編輯消耗 20 積分。該功能目前支援 Meshy 6 和 Meshy 7.1 生成的高精度模型；若模型帶有貼圖，系統會自動切換至未貼圖版本進行編輯。使用者可以在模型預覽視窗底部的“編輯”按鈕，或列印模組的後處理功能區找到入口。 關於 Meshy Meshy 由麻省理工學院博士胡淵鳴（Ethan Hu）創立，自研 AI 3D 生成基礎模型，於 2023 年釋出首個 Meshy 模型。使用者輸入一句文字、一張照片或一幅草圖，即可得到帶紋理、可直接匯出的 3D 資產，用於遊戲、影視、AR/VR、產品設計和 3D 列印。截至 2026 年 9 月，Meshy 全球註冊使用者超過 1500 萬，累計生成模型超過 1 億個。2026 年 7 月，Meshy 完成近 4 億美元 B 輪融資，估值 15 億美元；同年 9 月，年度經常性收入（ARR）突破 1 億美元。瞭解更多：meshy.ai 本文由Meshy提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 Meshy 量子位的朋友們 飛書豆包工作AI先鋒未來人才大賽：企業正在爭搶會用AI做成事的人 2026-10-21 比亞迪成為2026年APEC會議官方合作夥伴 2026-10-20 2026物理AI與世界模型大會醫療健康世界模型分會場在南京舉行 2026-10-19 技術賦能全球化深耕 比亞迪攜多品牌亮相2026巴黎車展 2026-10-20 相關閱讀

title: 賽豆首款AI汽車公告圖公示，價格被按零件猜到了20萬以上
abstract: 賽豆首款AI汽車公告圖公示，價格被按零件猜到了20萬以上 傑西卡 2026-10-20 12:18:29 來源： 量子位 寧德時代電池上車 傑西卡 發自 ROBO-車 量子位ROBO | 公眾號 AI4ROBO 千呼萬喚始出來啊！ 賽豆科技 首款車，亮相工信部了。 從申報圖和參數來看，正是此前在巴黎完成全球首秀的 AIVA ME7 。 這是一臺車長近5米、軸距超3米的中大型純電SUV，五座佈局，提供單電機、雙電機兩個版本，搭載寧德時代三元鋰電池，也是一臺從架構定義之初就是為AI而生的智慧汽車。 售價當然還沒有官方公佈，但外界目前已經有了猜測。 AIVA首款車亮相工信部 最近，工信部第412批新車公示目錄中，出現了賽豆的身影，新車申報圖和詳細參數隨之公開。 這款車採用轎跑SUV設計， 五座 佈局，整體姿態寬大低趴，前臉配有狹長的燈組，車頂可以看到雷射雷達。 尾部採用貫穿式尾燈，圍標也證實了這款車就是 AIVA ME7 。 車身尺寸上，AIVA ME7長寬高分別為 4999×1999×1616/1626mm ，軸距3050mm。 車長只差1mm就達到5米，寬度接近2米，軸距也超過3米，達到了中大型SUV的尺寸水平。 進一步看，新車前懸945mm、後懸1004mm，前後輪距分別達到1716mm和1722mm。 較長的軸距、相對緊湊的前後懸，能夠為車內空間佈局提供更多餘地；較寬的輪距配合低矮車身，則進一步強化了整車的運動姿態。 輪胎也採用了偏運動化的配置。申報資訊顯示，AIVA ME7提供20英寸和21英寸兩種輪圈規格。 其中，20英寸版本採用前255/50 R20、後275/50 R20輪胎；21英寸版本則升級為前265/45 R21、後285/45 R21。 也就是說，兩個版本的後輪都比前輪更寬，能夠為後軸提供更大的輪胎接地寬度。 動力方面，新車提供兩個版本： 單電機版本 最大功率 270kW ，約合367馬力，採用後輪驅動； 雙電機版本 則在此基礎上，增加一臺150kW的前電機，系統峰值功率合計達到 420kW ，約合571馬力。 兩個版本申報的最高車速均為255km/h。 電池方面，新車搭載的是 寧德時代 提供的 三元鋰電池 。 工信部還公佈了新車的整備質量。其中，單電機版本為2295kg或2370kg，雙電機版本則達到2425kg或2480kg，最重接近2.5噸。 除此之外，AIVA ME7還提供不同造型的輪圈、紅色制動卡鉗、黑色車頂等選裝配置，並申報了700kg的拖掛能力。 實際上，這並非AIVA ME7第一次公開亮相。 今年9月28日，AIVA ME7已經在法國巴黎完成 全球首秀 ，重點展示了外觀設計，以及部分智慧互動功能。 例如新車的“靈動光眸”，採用仿生設計和光點矩陣，能夠呈現不同的動態情緒表達能力，還能通過“眼神”變化回應車外人員的手勢。 AIVA ME7的車身還設計了十處導流風道，用於引導氣流經過車身，改善空氣動力學表現。 當然，AIVA此前最為強調的AI能力，還有一部分留在公告之外。例如智慧座艙、輔助駕駛方案、車載晶片等資訊，目前還沒有完整披露。 那麼這樣一臺AI汽車，到底什麼價位呢？ 一臺AI汽車，什麼價位？ 事實上，賽豆科技曾透露過AIVA的價格方向。 今年6月9日，AIVA品牌在北京正式釋出，提出了 “AI定義汽車，先有AI，再有車” 的造車路徑。彼時官方就明確，AIVA全系產品將覆蓋 20萬元以上主流市場 。 如今隨著工信部申報參數公開，目前外界也推測AIVA ME7的售價在20萬以上。 這個價格區間首先有品牌定位作為參考，同時，接近5米的中大型車身、雙電機四驅以及三元鋰電池，也對應著一定的產品規格。 而放眼20多萬元這個區間，市面上已經能買到配置相當豐富的純電SUV。800V甚至900V高壓平臺、超過700km的CLTC續航，以及越來越豐富的輔助駕駛功能，都已經出現在這個價位。 而且消費者關注的配置還在增加，除了續航和補能，車載大模型、智慧泊車、座椅舒適性、底盤控制等功能，也逐漸成為車企爭奪使用者的重要賣點。 也因此，這個價位已經聚集了一批技術和產品實力都不弱的車型。這也意味著，賽豆將直接闖入智慧電動車競爭最激烈的戰場。 不過，競爭最激烈的地方，往往也是機會最多的地方。20萬元以上既能容納中大型車身、更高規格的動力系統和智慧化硬體，又處於主流新能源汽車消費者可以考慮的價格範圍。 這個市場已經有成熟的消費需求，車型覆蓋家用、運動、智慧化等不同取向。消費者有更多產品可以選擇，新品牌也有機會憑藉不同的產品特色進入市場。 對於賽豆而言，AIVA進一步建立的差異，則主要落在 AI體驗 上。 根據此前的品牌規劃，AIVA將大模型能力融入汽車，為的是探索更加自然的人車互動，以及持續學習和迭代的智慧化功能。 通常來說，車企會先確定車型定位、目標使用者和主要使用場景，再圍繞空間、動力、智慧化等方面制定產品方案。 而AIVA提出了不同的產品思路——在整車定義之初，就將 AI能力 納入核心考量，圍繞AI重新設計人與汽車的互動方式。此前AIVA ME7在巴黎首秀中展示的燈光手勢互動，就是目前公開的一項嘗試。 後續隨著智慧座艙、輔助駕駛等更多資訊陸續披露，其AI能力可能也將成為消費者判斷產品價值的重要部分。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 賽豆科技 傑西卡 實探寧德時代總部：“去寧化”是喊太大聲了 2026-10-21 理想宣佈：電池自燃報廢賠新車！自研6年後有底氣了 2026-10-21 title: AI硬體出海，別當“背景板”，GTC2026 Shanghai「AI硬體專區」邀你佔位
abstract: AI硬體出海，別當“背景板”，GTC2026 Shanghai「AI硬體專區」邀你佔位 量子位的朋友們 2026-10-20 12:08:15 來源： 量子位 2026 年 11 月 4 日至 5 日，GTC2026 全球流量大會（上海）將在上海世博展覽館 H3 館舉辦 2026 年 11 月 4 日至 5 日，GTC2026 全球流量大會（上海）將在上海世博展覽館 H3 館舉辦，本屆展會特別設立「AI 硬體專區」 ，聚集機器人、智慧穿戴、AI 終端、具身智慧等方向的展商與從業者。目前，專區席位正在招募中，同時大會普通門票限時免費領取，歡迎所有對 AI 硬體出海感興趣的朋友報名參會。 一、AI硬體專區：把同路人聚在一起 「AI 硬體專區」是 GTC2026 Shanghai 為 AI 硬體賽道專門開闢的垂直展區。它不是一個簡單的展位集合，而是一個有明確主題、有精準觀眾、有配套活動的專屬場域。 專區覆蓋的方向包括：機器人、智慧穿戴裝置、AI 手機及終端、智慧家居硬體、具身智慧解決方案等。從整機品牌到技術方案，從產品公司到出海服務商，專區將把 AI 硬體出海的完整鏈條集中呈現。 在這裡，你的隔壁展位可能就是某家做陪伴機器人的團隊，對面可能是做智慧戒指或 AI 眼鏡的品牌。觀眾來到這個區域，目標非常明確：看產品、找合作、聊渠道走進來的人，本來就衝著 AI 硬體來的。 專區還將與大會的 AI 相關議程形成聯動。11 月 5 日上午的主會場「AI+出海峰會」，將深入討論 AI 產品從工具到智慧體的進化路徑、AI 應用的商業化與變現手段；11 月 4 日下午的分會場「AI 技術發展論壇」，則聚焦 AI Agent 落地、AI 出海基建、軟體生產新範式等硬核技術話題。展區與論壇彼此呼應，讓參展企業既能展示產品，也能吸收前沿認知。 二、為什麼這個專區值得AI硬體從業者專門來一趟？ 對於 AI 硬體企業來說，參加展會的核心訴求無非是幾個：找到渠道、對接供應鏈、接觸投資人、提升品牌聲量。而「AI 硬體專區」恰恰把這些需求集中到了一個高濃度的場景裡。 如果你是 AI 硬體企業，想參展： 專區匯聚的觀眾不是泛泛的“逛展人群”，而是帶著明確需求的渠道方、採購方、海外代理商、投資機構以及出海服務商。GTC2026 Shanghai 預計將迎來 1800+企業高管、120+優質展商、15000+行業從業者。專區企業可以獲得更精準的曝光，同時與大會全鏈路的支付合規、本地化服務、雲基建、營銷推廣等展商直接對接，一站式解決出海路上多個環節的難題。 如果你是 AI 硬體從業者，想參會： 你可以在這裡一次性看到當前 AI 硬體出海企業的最新成果，瞭解同行在做什麼、市場在流行什麼。你也可以參與AI+出海峰會和技術發展論壇，聽一線操盤手拆解AI硬體出海的真實案例——哪些市場在起量、哪些渠道值得投入、合規和本地化有哪些坑。你還可以在專區裡認識潛在的合作夥伴，無論是找渠道，還是找技術方案，這裡的人都和你處在同一個賽道。 如果你是渠道方、投資人或服務商： AI 硬體專區是你集中接觸優質專案的入口，專區讓你在最短時間內完成專案篩選和初步對接。你可以在現場體驗產品、與團隊深入交流，甚至直接敲定合作意向。 三、報名通道已開啟，多場次峰會、活動等您蒞臨 開幕式峰會暨鯨鳴獎頒獎典禮｜11 月 4 日上午 這是整個大會的定調之場，也是全年出海圈的高光時刻。開幕式將匯聚政府代表、行業領袖與出海頭部企業，共同解讀 2026 全球市場的最新風向。更重要的是， 第八屆鯨鳴獎頒獎典禮將在此舉行 。鯨鳴獎已連續舉辦七屆，累計 750+企業站上領獎臺，覆蓋行業受眾超 200000+。九大獎項涵蓋優秀出海遊戲廠商、全球影響力短劇出海平臺、AI 生態技術創新企業、影響力出海品牌、卓越出海領軍人物等。誰將成為今年的出海標杆？現場揭曉。對於正在尋找行業背書的品牌來說，這不僅是榮譽，更是一次被全行業看見的機會。 遊戲出海峰會｜11 月 4 日下午 遊戲出海早已不是“買量換增長”的粗放時代。歐美市場合規門檻抬高，日韓使用者對本地化要求苛刻，中東、拉美雖有增量但支付和運營成本高企。本場峰會將聚焦產業投資視角、區域市場二次進場、混合變現調優、休閒遊戲突圍等實戰議題。來自一線發行商和研發團隊的操盤手，將拆解真實案例——不是“我們做對了什麼”，而是“我們踩過哪些坑，以及怎麼爬出來的”。如果你正在尋找下一款爆款，或者想調整產品策略，這場峰會是成本最低的一次外部覆盤。 title: ✅China’s Draft AI Export Controls Don’t Block Open-Weight Models
abstract: On October 16, China’s Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and Ministry of Science and Technology (MOST) released a draft addition to the country’s catalogue of technologies restricted or prohibited from export. For the first time , the proposal covers advanced large AI models, AI agents and massive computing clusters. Anything on the list would either be barred from leaving China or require a license. The draft names 40 key technologies across AI, biopharma and photovoltaic technologies (used to manufacture solar panels). 14 are prohibited while 26 are restricted and would need permission to export. The ministries are taking public comment from Oct 16 to Nov 15, therefore this is a draft, not a final rule. While the draft is under consultation, a temporary registration is required for exports of the listed technologies, including transactions underway but not yet completed. It covers overseas ownership transfers and licensing, as well as changes that place domestically held technology under foreign ownership or actual control. You can find the original Chinese text here. The Geopolitechs newsletter published an insightful analysis ended with a few great open questions. In this issue, I’ll focus primarily on the listed AI models, agents and computing infrastructure and debunk some myths circulating on social media. The prohibited AI technologies covers models trained using China’s legally designated “core data,” which refers to data involving national security, the lifelines of the national economy, major aspects of people's livelihoods, or major public interests. Also prohibited from export are agents for highly sensitive applications (like national defense and military), advanced offensive cyber technologies featuring AI-driven malware generation and mutation , and certain deepfake-detection technologies for cross-border data security. Models trained on “important data” fall into the restricted category, subject to exceptions. This compromise of important data could endanger national security, economic operations, social stability, or public interests. So does any model that meets one of three thresholds: Training computation ≥10²⁶ floating-point operations . Globally leading capability, defined through top-10 public assessments at the time of export. Those assessments can include specialized capabilities, usage, safety, or training efficiency—not just overall performance. Covered technologies include weights, checkpoints, source code, architecture, and training and inference optimizations. Agents are judged on autonomy and intended use. Restricted agents include systems meeting combined thresholds for decomposing tasks into at least 20 steps, coordinating at least 60 agents, or integrating at least 200 tools, alongside specified accuracy, efficiency, and success rates. Advanced strategic decision-making agents are also covered. Other restricted AI-related technologies include AI and memory-chip design, computing systems with more than 10,000 AI accelerator cards, AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and exploitation, and advanced detection, voiceprint recognition, and translation. The draft adds two explicit footnotes. First, technology already in the public domain through open source, academic publication, or similar means is outside the export controls’ scope. Second, for restricted AI technologies , open-source release, Chinese companies’ self-built and self-operated overseas computing centers, overseas chip fabrication, joint R&D using overseas resources, and international standards work would receive automatic licensing or other facilitation . This means the draft export control would not block open weight releases. MOFCOM’s press spokesperson said that most AI technologies would remain freely exportable. Using restricted models to provide overseas users with API access, app or web interactions, SaaS applications, or lightweight on-device deployments would not be applicable within the export controls. Simply speaking, providing restricted models as a service is fine. Overseas deployment of restricted AI technologies, however, would fall within the export controls, although deployment on a Chinese company’s own overseas cloud could qualify for automatic licensing. I read three motives in the ministry’s explanation. First is AI safety. Here is what MOFCOM said: First, to ensure that AI technology remains safe and controllable. Countries worldwide are increasingly concerned about the risks inherent in AI and those arising from its use. Technologies proposed for control, such as AI-driven autonomous generation and mutation of malicious code, could be used to attack sensitive systems—including critical national information infrastructure, defense and military industries, and core government systems—or to circumvent national security defenses. If acquired by non-state actors or malicious entities, these technologies could threaten national security and humanity’s collective security. The Chinese government’s purpose in placing necessary controls on such technologies is to uphold essential safeguards, prevent misuse and malicious use, ensure that AI remains under human control at all times, and advance international AI governance. AI-driven malicious code tools could be used against critical infrastructure, defense and core government systems, and could be dangerous in the hands of non-state actors. The government’s goal is keeping AI under human control. It frames this against a rising number of cybersecurity incidents, including a recent case where OpenAI’s agents reportedly broke into multiple governments’ systems. Second is openness with a line drawn. Here is what MOFCOM said: The Chinese government is committed to making AI an important driver of shared prosperity and collective security. To support an open-source AI innovation ecosystem, technology exports involving the open-sourcing of AI technologies, Chinese companies building and operating their own computing centers overseas, chip tape-out and manufacturing abroad, joint R&D using overseas resources, and participation in international standards development will qualify for facilitation measures such as automatic licensing, effectively allowing exports to proceed upon filing. Relevant technologies that have already entered the public domain through open-source releases, academic publications, or similar means are proposed to fall outside the scope of export controls, creating a favorable environment for international exchange and cooperation in AI. The Chinese government wants to be seen backing open source. But there is a line. Open-weight release and a company’s own overseas data centers could get approval. But deploying a restricted model with over 2 trillion parameters inside someone else’s infrastructure may not. By that logic, my reading is a Kimi K3 deployment on Microsoft Azure would likely need a pre-approval going forward. Third is preventing another Manus acquisition. The Chinese government blocked Meta's acquisition of AI agent startup Manus this April. The government appears to want a way to stop critical technology from leaving China as a company relocates. At the same time, they do not want to hurt the service side as AI is playing a vital role in boosting China’s export economy growth. China’s draft export control is unique for setting thresholds on models and agents directly, alongside controls on chips and compute. Most existing AI export controls worldwide target the compute supply chain. U.S.: Requires licenses for specified advanced AI chips, computing systems and semiconductor-production technologies going to China and other restricted destinations or users. Restrictions also address military uses and diversion through third countries. The Biden administration’s January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule included controls on advanced closed-model weights, but the Trump administration announced its rescission in May 2025.

title: Mistral Advances AI for Engineering with NVIDIA
abstract: Company Mistral Advances AI for Engineering with NVIDIA October 21, 2026 By Mistral Back to Blog 5 min read Share this post Copy url to clipboard Copied Thinking Summary Mistral and NVIDIA are collaborating to revolutionize engineering workflows by integrating Mistral’s AI models with NVIDIA’s accelerated computing and physics modeling tools, enabling faster simulations and closed-loop AI-driven design. The partnership will introduce public benchmarks and open datasets to standardize evaluations for physics and agentic AI in computer-aided engineering, while leveraging NVIDIA’s Omniverse for 3D simulation and asset creation. Building on their existing work, including the development of Mistral Large 4, the initiative aims to push the boundaries of AI-powered engineering across industries like aerospace, automotive, and semiconductors. Mistral is collaborating with NVIDIA to develop a new generation of AI-native engineering workflows powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing. Combining Mistral Large 4 , with Mistral’s data generation, and physics modeling pipelines, accelerated by NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries and NVIDIA Warp , the initiative aims to accelerate engineering simulation and enable closed-loop workflows that connect simulation, AI model development and engineering design. Mistral and NVIDIA will also work together to integrate Mistral's models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for GPU-accelerated 3D scene generation and SimReady asset creation. A central focus of the collaboration is the development of public benchmarks and open datasets for evaluating physics models. These benchmarks will give researchers, developers and industrial teams a shared foundation to compare model accuracy and performance and build and validate automated CAD-to-simulation workflows. "For too long, the pace of engineering has been set by the pace of simulation. With Mistral's open-weight models and physics AI capabilities, combined with NVIDIA’s accelerated computing stack, we’re giving engineers faster simulation cycles, as well as open benchmarks rigorous enough to validate agents on real CAE and EDA work.” Neil Ashton, VP of Computational Engineering, Mistral Beyond physics AI, Mistral and NVIDIA will also work together to develop dedicated evaluations and benchmarks for agentic AI in computer-aided engineering (CAE) and electronic design automation (EDA) to accelerate the application of AI for engineering within aerospace, automotive and semiconductor use-cases. These benchmarks will assess agents’ ability to use engineering tools, complete multistep workflows and produce technically correct results, while measuring execution time and computational cost. Through this work, Mistral and NVIDIA will help define standards for agentic and physics AI evaluations in engineering, establishing consistent, reproducible methods for assessing capabilities and tracking progress. Powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, libraries and tools, Mistral will redefine AI for engineering, transforming how engineers design, simulate and build the next generation of products. “The next wave of engineering breakthroughs will come from exploring ideas that were once too complex or time-consuming to test,” said Tim Costa, vice president and general manager of industrial and computational engineering at NVIDIA. “By combining Mistral’s advanced open models and deep expertise in physics AI with NVIDIA accelerated computing and libraries, we’re helping engineers push the boundaries of design—with shared industry benchmarks to build confidence in what AI can do.” Building on the ongoing NVIDIA and Mistral partnership The industrial engineering collaboration builds on an ongoing partnership between NVIDIA and Mistral spanning open model development, domain-specific AI and the infrastructure needed to bring these capabilities into production. The companies previously co-developed Mistral NeMo and are now working together through the NVIDIA Nemotron Coalition to develop a frontier base model that will continue to advance the open weight frontier. This shared foundation will enable developers and enterprises worldwide to specialize AI for their industries, languages and regions, supported by contributions of data, evaluations and domain expertise from coalition members. Mistral recently introduced the public preview of Mistral Large 4 , known as Le Chonk, its largest and most capable frontier model to date. With approximately 1 trillion total parameters and 49 billion active parameters, the multimodal model was trained on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral-operated data centers in Europe. It advances capabilities across coding, agentic workflows and multimodal understanding, with weights planned for release at the end of October. Alongside model development, Mistral and NVIDIA are expanding the infrastructure that powers AI training, customization and inference. Mistral is bringing additional NVIDIA-powered AI infrastructure online in support of Mistral’s compute roadmap targeting 1 GW of capacity by 2030. This expansion strengthens Europe’s role in developing and delivering AI for the world. By connecting European infrastructure and research with open models, specialized engineering capabilities and customer applications, Mistral and NVIDIA are helping enterprises build AI around their own expertise and scale it to serve markets worldwide. 0%

title: Solving a 31-year-old grand challenge in mathematics – the KLS conjecture
abstract: For decades, a fundamental question about the difficulty of computing in high-dimensional spaces has resisted proof. New research resolves this question, removing a major theoretical obstacle to understanding the efficiency of randomized algorithms used across science and computing. The Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits (KLS) conjecture was proposed in 1995. It asks whether, for a broad class of high-dimensional probability distributions, the best flat or hyperplane cut is always nearly as effective as the best cut of any shape. More precisely, KLS predicts that the two differ by no more than a universal constant, regardless of the number of dimensions. This would establish a dimension-free geometric principle with important consequences for high-dimensional geometry, probability, and theoretical computer science. Because the geometry of these cuts governs how quickly random walks can explore a distribution, KLS also plays a central role in the theory of high-dimensional sampling. Since 1995, mathematicians have accumulated evidence that the conjecture was true, but a complete proof remained elusive. Now, two researchers, including Xinzhi Zhang from the Machine Learning and Optimization group at Microsoft Research, have proved the KLS conjecture (opens in new tab) . They have shown that the relationship holds with a fixed bound, regardless of how many dimensions a shape has. Before this work, the best known result (opens in new tab) , established in July 2026, allowed that bound to grow slowly as the number of dimensions increased. This work establishes a fundamental geometric principle: high-dimensional spaces are better behaved than previously known, and the obstacles to navigating them do not grow without bound as dimensions increase. The importance of the KLS conjecture was recognized across the field long before it was resolved. In its 2017-18 Annual Report, the Mathematical Sciences Research Institute (MSRI) (opens in new tab) called it “a central open problem in high-dimensional convex geometry.” The Simons Institute (opens in new tab) described it as “one of the most important open problems in convex geometry.” In the proceedings of the 2022 International Congress of Mathematicians (ICM) (opens in new tab) , Ronen Eldan noted its broad implications for high-dimensional convex and computational geometry. Quanta Magazine (opens in new tab) wrote that KLS “lies at the heart of many questions in statistics and computer science.” The authors began by improving the July 2026 result in order to make the mathematical bound more precise. Working with AI agents in a structured, human-directed process, they explored more than 100 candidate approaches, many involving lengthy calculations with higher-order tensors. This produced a new mathematical criterion that became the foundation of the final proof. The authors then discovered that the new criterion could be applied recursively. Each improved bound could be fed back into the same argument to produce a still tighter one. In the October 1, 2026 version of the paper, this reduced the dependence on dimension to the iterated logarithm. This function grows extraordinarily slowly, but it still grows with the dimension and therefore did not yet fully resolve the conjecture. The final step was to repeat the entire recursive refinement, rather than applying it only once. This idea was inspired by the authors’ earlier work on fast algorithms for linear programming. The authors proved that the small errors introduced at each stage shrink fast enough that their total remains bounded by a universal constant, independent of the dimension. This eliminated the dependence on the number of dimensions and completed the proof in the October 4, 2026 version of the paper. The recursive method, its repeated application, and the proof that the accumulated errors remain bounded are original contributions of the researchers. AI tools helped explore candidate approaches, carry out detailed derivations, prepare the manuscript, and perform internal proof checks. The researchers determined the mathematical direction, selected the promising ideas, assembled them into the final argument, and verified the proof. On the same day that the authors posted their complete proof, a separate group of leading experts posted a full proof (opens in new tab) that they developed in parallel. Their work built upon the findings in the first version (opens in new tab) of the Microsoft paper, calling it “the crucial step in the proof.” A third proof (opens in new tab) which appeared separately on the same day relies on a closely related idea. In addition, a Lean 4 formalization (opens in new tab) was subsequently released, combining the key criterion from the first Microsoft paper with additional research. Independent proofs are among mathematics’ strongest forms of validation because they demonstrate that a result does not rest on a single chain of reasoning. The subsequent appearance of alternative approaches and formal verification further strengthens confidence that the field has uncovered a genuine underlying principle rather than a fragile technical argument. The authors have also shortened their proof and verified the streamlined argument in Lean; they plan to release both after final review. Together, these developments provide complementary forms of confirmation. In the process of proving KLS, this research also demonstrates the power of having researchers direct AI rather than simply asking AI to solve a complex problem through a single end-to-end run of a frontier model or agent. The authors used an agentic search process with iterative, human-assisted “pruning”: As multiple agents explored variations of an idea in parallel, the researcher examined their intermediate result, eliminated unpromising directions, and passed the most promising result to the next round. Roughly one hundred research trajectories were explored before the key breakthrough emerged. In a separate track of the project, the authors made repeated unguided attempts to solve the same problem with several leading AI models, using roughly the same total token budget as the main process. That effort fell short of the goal. The eventual success depended on both the capabilities of the AI systems and the mathematical judgment of the researchers. Taken together, resolving KLS settles a central problem in high-dimensional geometry. A wide range of results that previously relied on the conjecture as an assumption can now be stated unconditionally. The proof therefore provides a stronger foundation for research in convex geometry, probability, and theoretical computer science. The work also demonstrates how carefully guided human-AI collaboration can contribute to genuine scientific discovery while reinforcing, rather than replacing human insight. It highlights the continuing importance of scientific judgment in identifying promising directions, recognizing conceptual connections, and seeing when a partial insight points toward a deeper result. The authors are now simplifying the proof and extending its formal verification so that the mathematics and theoretical computer science communities can more easily examine the result and build on it. Thank you to our co-author Zhao Song for his contributions to this work, and Victor Reis (opens in new tab) and Ishai Menache for helpful discussions throughout the project. The post Solving a 31-year-old grand challenge in mathematics – the KLS conjecture appeared first on Microsoft Research .

title: Databricks AI Runtime and NVIDIA make it easier to customize open models with enterprise data
abstract: GPUs power today's most advanced AI workloads, from cutting-edge language models to multimodal AI systems and agents. Increasingly, enterprises are adapting open models to their own data and business needs. But securing GPU access is only part of the challenge. Teams also need to configure training jobs, govern data access, and manage GPU infrastructure, leaving less time to experiment with models and evaluate how well they meet business needs. Databricks and NVIDIA provide a seamless path from enterprise data to customized AI models, from fine-tuning smaller models to large-scale distributed training. Through Unity Gateway, Databricks provides developers with governed access to frontier and open-source models. For teams that need to customize models, AI Runtime (AIR) brings NVIDIA’s AI software ecosystem and serverless GPUs to enterprise data. Teams can experiment, fine-tune, and evaluate models on AIR, then deploy them for real-time inference through Databricks Model Serving — all within the Databricks Platform, with less infrastructure and governance work to manage. Today at GTC Berlin, Databricks and NVIDIA are expanding their collaboration to make it easier for enterprises to customize open models. Databricks AIR is now generally available : developers can use NVIDIA NeMo, NGC containers, and new Nemotron cookbooks to train and fine-tune open models on serverless NVIDIA GPUs. Together, these capabilities give teams more flexibility to adapt models to business-specific tasks and put them to work in applications and agents. AIR provides serverless NVIDIA GPUs for training and fine-tuning, so developers can run their existing code and containers at scale without managing GPU infrastructure. With support for multi-node distributed training, teams can scale larger workloads across GPU nodes. NVIDIA Quantum InfiniBand provides high-bandwidth, low-latency networking with remote direct memory access (RDMA), while NVIDIA Collective Communications Library (NCCL) handles communication between GPUs. Databricks manages the underlying clusters and networking. For example, an enterprise building a technical support agent could start with an NVIDIA Nemotron open model and fine-tune it on labeled support tickets using NVIDIA NeMo on AIR. The team could experiment with different training approaches and use MLflow to track results as they adapt the model to their specific support workflows. Developers can prepare Lakehouse data and experiment in GPU-powered notebooks or through the AIR CLI, using high-performance data loading and standard environments that include PyTorch and CUDA. They can use distributed training frameworks or bring their own libraries and custom training loops. When experiments are ready for repeatable execution, Lakeflow Jobs can orchestrate training alongside upstream data preparation and downstream evaluation, turning individual runs into repeatable workflows. Declarative Automation Bundles support CI/CD for deploying and updating those workflows. MLflow tracks training experiments and GPU utilization, helping teams compare model results and compute performance. Unity Catalog governs access to training data, and native system tables provide visibility into CPU and GPU usage. Together, these integrations let teams use the data, governance, and operational tools they already rely on in Databricks. Training and fine-tuning deep learning models takes more than GPU compute—teams also need flexibility in their frameworks, libraries, and environments. AIR now supports Docker and private registries, allowing developers to bring custom containerized environments to their GPU workloads. Developers can use GPU-optimized containers from the NVIDIA NGC Catalog with the Databricks Artifact Registry to bring NVIDIA software into AIR. Environment caching helps these workloads start quickly, reducing setup overhead as teams iterate on training code and rerun experiments. Developers can also install NVIDIA profiling tools to examine GPU execution and investigate performance bottlenecks. Alongside GPU utilization metrics tracked in MLflow, these tools help teams understand where training workloads spend time and identify opportunities to improve performance. Teams can tune their software and training code while AIR manages the underlying GPU infrastructure. AIR supports customization beyond LLMs, including a validated fine-tuning workflow for NVIDIA Kumo Anomaly , an open research model for time-series anomaly detection, with MLflow tracking and Unity Catalog checkpoints. This supports NVIDIA’s Agent Knowledge Foundation vision of building an agent knowledge layer. Pairing Kumo-Anomaly with the Genie Ontology offers a path to context-aware agents that connect unusual patterns in time-series data with business meaning to help inform next steps. With the release of Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and Super VL, Databricks customers can load, experiment with, adapt, and serve these models on Databricks from day one. AIR supports model customization with NVIDIA NeMo and NeMo Automodel , enabling teams to use NVIDIA’s tools and frameworks on serverless NVIDIA GPUs. In the technical support agent example, this means developers could use these tools to fine-tune Nemotron on historical support tickets, helping the model better understand company-specific products, terminology, and troubleshooting workflows. Training stays connected to enterprise data and workflows in Databricks. Genie Code can also help developers author and adapt the training script directly in a notebook. Developers can describe the changes they need, ask for help configuring a fine-tuning run, and work through errors as they arise. They can review and refine the suggested code before running it on serverless NVIDIA GPUs. For fine-tuning, AIR combines optimized data loading, checkpointing, and training with integrated observability and debugging tools. Developers can track experiments and GPU metrics in MLflow and use Genie Code to: After fine-tuning and evaluation, teams can deploy customized models to production through Databricks Model Serving. In our technical support example, the fine-tuned Nemotron model could power an agent that interprets incoming support requests and generates responses informed by the company's products and troubleshooting workflows. This completes the workflow from model customization on serverless NVIDIA GPUs to real-time inference. To learn more, visit our web page , AIR documentation , and explore the Nemotron 3.5 SuperVL and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning cookbooks to get started with GPU training and fine-tuning on Databricks. title: AI Runtime is Generally Available
abstract: Today, we’re excited to announce the General Availability of AI Runtime (AIR), bringing fully managed GPU infrastructure directly into Databricks so customers can train their most demanding models where their enterprise data already lives. Too often, AI teams spend more time securing GPU capacity, managing failures, and waiting for experiments to launch than improving their models. Running GPU infrastructure separately from their Lakehouse adds governance gaps and puts sensitive training data at risk. As coding agents drive more training experiments , these bottlenecks and risks grow — making reliable, fast, and governed infrastructure essential. AIR brings GPU infrastructure, developer tools, and data governance together so teams can train at scale, iterate faster, and secure every workload without managing a separate GPU stack. Hundreds of companies, including Robinhood, PicPay, Merck, Flo Health , TinyFish , and FactSet , already use AIR to train and ship deep learning models to production, with use cases spanning healthcare, manufacturing, and consumer-facing agents. Our own Databricks AI Research team uses AIR to train the models behind KARL and AI Parse. Managing GPU infrastructure requires significant operational overhead, from capacity planning and node maintenance to networking and monitoring. With AIR, Databricks takes on the operational work of provisioning GPUs, maintaining healthy infrastructure, and optimizing the workload, so your team can focus on training: Access GPUs via CLI or interactively within Notebooks or IDEs. Your first workload just requires a single CLI command. With Databricks AIR Skills , migrating from a K8S or SLURM cluster just takes a single natural language prompt. Orchestrate GPU workloads with confidence with Lakeflow AIR integrates natively with Lakeflow so you can keep GPU workloads in sync with upstream and downstream pipelines. Moving to production requires just a few extra lines of YAML, with built in priority/pre-emption that minimize idle GPU time and monitoring tools like Genie ZeroOps that lower operational toil. Distributed training workloads are painful to set up and launch. AI teams waste time configuring training environments, waiting for GPU clusters to spin up, and debugging issues across the stack. AIR helps you get from code to training in seconds. You can use pre-built environments or bring your own container , and benefit from highly optimized environment caching so you just need to build environments once. AIR is compatible with all major frameworks, including Ray, so you can bring code over with minimal configuration. Launch your next experiment in seconds When you iterate and develop a training script, every second of delay is felt repeatedly. And so, we’ve optimized every layer of the provisioning stack to make workloads, even large scale RDMA-enabled clusters with dozens of GPUs, spin up in seconds. Debug distributed training in one place We’ve built an entirely new observability experience in MLflow, the industry’s leading experiment tracking tool. With this new experience, debugging your logs, which stream seconds after submission, is as simple as adding –watch to your AIR command. For deeper investigation, you can use our new logs viewer, tailor-built for multinode training. Agentic debugging with built-in Genie Code Genie Code is embedded into the entire user experience, and comes pre-packaged with agent skills to help you debug issues and optimize GPU training performance. These skills include insights that our research and performance teams discover, like how we reduced Qwen training time by 6x on AIR . Managing GPU infrastructure separately from enterprise data creates governance gaps, fragmented access controls, and unnecessary data copies. As agents run hundreds of training experiments in parallel, teams need to ensure sensitive data stays governed and workloads remain securely isolated, without relying on manual oversight. The OpenAI Huggingface incident underscores this risk. AIR extends your trusted data controls and governance to every GPU workload. Unity Catalog enforces consistent read/write permissions on all aspects of a GPU workload (data access, checkpoints, logs, etc.), so your GPU platform and data governance layer now speak the exact same language. Isolate workloads and control network access AIR is backed by years of investment in serverless security , isolation, and private networking. Unlike GPU isolation mechanisms that expose the host kernel, AIR has VM-level isolation, supports PrivateLink and serverless egress controls. Thus AIR offers much stronger protections for training workloads compared to conventional systems. Understand where your GPU budget goes Track AIR usage and costs through Databricks billing system tables , alongside your other Databricks workloads. Use workload-level usage records to identify which training workloads consume your GPU budget and guide decisions about future runs. To help you get started, we’ve put together several template notebooks and starter guides: Please reach out to your account team to learn more or if you have any questions! title: Deploy RFD4-Proteina on Databricks
abstract: Bring RFD4-Proteina to your research data with AI-assisted development and serverless NVIDIA GPU compute. RFD4-Proteina, an NVIDIA BioNeMo open model co-developed with the University of Washington Institute for Protein Design, helps scientists turn ideas for useful proteins into designs they can test. NVIDIA and Databricks are bringing the model into Genesis Workbench on AI Runtime, giving developers a path to connect protein-design workflows with their research data. Databricks AI Runtime (AIR) provides serverless NVIDIA GPU compute for supported workloads. The planned integration connects model execution with research data and repeatable workflows on Databricks, reducing the infrastructure overhead required to evaluate and adapt a new model. Putting a model to work requires more than downloading weights. Developers need to prepare inputs, connect scientific tools, configure execution, and track results—all while protecting proprietary data. Databricks brings these steps into a shared environment, reducing the need to assemble and maintain a separate research stack. RFD4-Proteina builds on the approach used in Proteina-Complexa, NVIDIA's generative model for designing protein binders that co-generates amino-acid sequences and all-atom structures in a single pass. RFD4-Proteina extends that joint generation approach with optional reward-guided search, letting researchers steer candidate design toward properties like thermostability or binding affinity. The planned integration expands on Genesis Workbench’s existing Proteina-Complexa workflows patterns,utilizing scoring models withreward functions specific to the problem at hand. Genesis Workbench has two built-in workflows using RFD4-Proteina for your reference: Antibody Design and Vaccine Design. Pictured : Antibody Design in Genesis Workbench with NVIDIA RFD4-Proteina Genesis Workbench offers an easy way to get started: its open, modular blueprint illustrates how to connect biological models with input preparation, candidate evaluation, and downstream analysis on Databricks. Developers can reuse individual components or adapt the implementation to their own scientific methods. Teams can store model weights in Unity Catalog volumes as governed MLflow models and reuse them across experiments. Teams can register fine-tuned models in Unity Catalog through MLflow, connecting model versions with configurations and artifacts. Access controls and network configuration should reflect where the model, scoring tools, and coding agents execute. Using RFD4-Proteina through Genesis Workbench gives Databricks users the broader ability to connect research across disciplines: genomics analysis can inform a target, single-cell data can provide biological context, and protein-design or small-molecule workflows can support subsequent investigation. Genesis Workbench provides examples of these capabilities within a shared environment. Databricks Genie Code helps developers build, debug, and adapt data and ML workflows using natural language. NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit skills add specialized instructions, scripts, and references for biological models and scientific tools, including structure prediction, protein design, molecular docking, and genomics analysis. These skills can help a coding agent prepare inputs, invoke supported tools, inspect outputs, and assemble multi-step workflows. Developers can combine that guidance with their own data conventions, evaluation criteria, and experiment-tracking requirements. Genesis Workbench also provides skills for Claude-based coding agents, offering another entry point: helping developers understand the blueprint, scaffold integrations for new models such as RFD4-Proteina , and tailor those integrations to a specific use case. This can accelerate the first implementation; dependency checks, testing, and scientific review remain part of the process. A life science researcher could leverage prebuilt RFD4-Proteina workflows directly from Genesis Workbench or use Genie Code to create a Databricks Notebook for an ad-hoc experiment with a simple english prompt like: “Design a nanobody (VHH) against PD-L1 using RFD4-Proteina framework conditioning: keep a real humanized framework (h-NbBCII10) fixed and design only the CDR loops onto the PD-1-blocking epitope. Run 8 iterations × 8 samples with ProteinMPNN on the CDRs and Boltz co-folding for binding; weight the reward toward binding (ipTM), fold confidence (pLDDT), developability (solubility, thermostability), and low anti-drug-antibody risk (MHC-II). Return the top designs with the reward trajectory and top-K complex PDBs." Genie Code assists with implementation, while developers and researchers retain control by reviewing the code, selecting appropriate tools, and interpreting results. AIR simplifies access to NVIDIA acceleration without requiring teams to provision and maintain separate GPU clusters. Developers can connect a notebook to Serverless GPU compute, select an NVIDIA H100 accelerator and a supported environment, and run their workload. The documented setup includes selecting the accelerator and base environment before applying the configuration. This reduces the work of configuring GPU infrastructure and maintaining a base software environment,though teams still need to validate model-specific libraries and dependencies. For supported biological foundation models, teams can also adapt BioNeMo Recipes to train or fine-tune on proprietary data using AIR’s serverless GPUs. BioNeMo Recipes provide reference implementations for accelerated training with familiar frameworks such as PyTorch and Hugging Face. Lakeflow orchestration, MLflow experiment tracking, and Unity Catalog governance connect execution to repeatable workflows and enterprise controls. Scientists can focus more on biology, while developers and platform teams spend less time managing infrastructure. An example practical model lifecycle on Databricks can include: For supported custom-model endpoints, scale-to-zero can reduce provisioned capacity during inactivity. Cold starts add latency, and GPU capacity is not guaranteed when an endpoint scales back up. Databricks recommends disabling scale-to-zero for workloads requiring consistent availability or response times. Teams can choose the execution pattern that fits the research task, balancing runtime, cost, and availability requirements. Across the workflow, teams can retain the configuration, model version, evaluation results, and artifacts needed to compare experiments. Computational evaluation supports candidate prioritization; laboratory validation remains essential. Explore the Genesis Workbench repository and begin with one target, a defined design objective, and a small experiment. Use the example implementation and available agent skills to adapt the workflow, then execute and track it on AIR before expanding. title: A new plugin can enable fast runtime monitoring and control
abstract: A lot happens under the hood as an LLM acts on an incoming prompt and formulates a response. Hardly any of this generative processing, though, shows up in the text that ultimately reaches users. You can make visible an LLM’s hidden ‘thought’ process using various tools for interpreting and steering AI model behavior, but most are incompatible with inference engines optimized for speed. In production environments where a model’s safety, tone, and accuracy matter most, these safety tools typically introduce long delays. That leaves two alternatives: training lightweight adapters to handle specific issues or retraining the model and recomputing its weights. IBM’s new plugin library moves away from tinkering with models, and instead, targets the inference engine serving them up. Called vLLM-Hook MIA , it’s designed to let developers observe and steer a model’s evolving states at runtime, to do things like decline a malicious prompt, flag ‘hallucinated’ facts, or edit a response for tone and accuracy, all while hardly slowing down performance. MIA (model internals aperture) is designed for vLLM , the main open-source inference engine serving enterprise workloads today. In a new technical report , IBM researchers reported that vLLM-Hook MIA was up to 20 times faster than its predecessor, vLLM-Hook, and up to 14 times faster than a similar method that inserts code into the model to interact with it. “We show that you can observe and intervene in an AI model’s generation process without a major lag in performance,” says Irene Ko, an IBM researcher who leads the vLLM-Hook project. “We hope this can make running last-minute safety checks in vLLM more practical.” Speed versus transparency Today’s inference engines were engineered for speed, and one of their core performance features is something called graph capture and replay, typically implemented using NVIDIA’s CUDA Graphs. vLLM captures repetitive execution steps, like the decode phase forward pass, into a fixed execution graph. Then, instead of launching GPU kernels one by one, the runtime sends a single graph replay command, reducing CPU bottlenecks. This efficiency feature is key to vLLM’s high throughput. It’s also what makes monitoring and steering an LLM at runtime so difficult. To inspect or change a model’s neural activations, many interpretability tools need to run Python code within each model layer. You can only do this in vLLM, however, by disabling graph capture and replay and shifting into its “eager” execution mode. In search of a workaround, IBM researchers homed in on graph replay. In MIA, the latest version of vLLM-Hook, GPU operators capture and steer model internals before the graph is recorded. A “scheduler” and a “courier” then manage access to internal states and data flows without interrupting vLLM’s efficient processing. A developer specifies which model internals they want to capture or steer, and the scheduler translates those selections into routing entries stored at fixed GPU memory addresses. During graph replay, the GPU uses those entries to act on the developer’s request. The courier then moves the captured data to CPU memory to deliver with the model’s output. We hope this can make running last-minute safety checks in vLLM more practical. Shifting interpretability tools from research to production Like many new technologies, vLLM-Hook started with a problem. In collaboration with their colleagues, Ko and Pin-Yu Chen, an IBM researcher focused on AI safety, had developed an attention tracking tool to identify prompts potentially intended to trick models into divulging information they shouldn’t. Chen’s tracker analyzes a model’s attention patterns at inference time and picks out deviations indicating it could be about to ignore its guardrails. In research environments, the attention tracker worked fine. Production was another matter. “I said it was a great idea, but making it work in vLLM was going to be painful,” said David Cox, an IBM vice president who leads AI development. “They took the comment to heart and started building extension points to vLLM.” Working with Chen, and Yunhua Fang, an extern studying at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, Chen saw that inserting Python ‘hooks’ into the decoder layers of a model’s forward pass could make visible vLLM’s generation process. With a few snippets of code, they could pick and capture a model’s evolving states, a bit like a tape recorder programmed to record at designated moments. You could either ‘read’ those selected states or ‘write’ over them to improve a model’s response. The team released the first version of vLLM-Hook earlier this year. When they ran their attention tracker, they saw a 1.7-times speedup over the Hugging Face transformers library, where many research tools are first deployed. To further improve performance, they searched for a way to access the model’s internal states without turning off graph replay, vLLM’s fast execution mode. MIA was the result. In experiments, Chen and Ko showed that using vLLM-Hook-MIA to steer relatively small models, an 8B Llama and Qwen 1.5B model, inferencing was delayed by just 2% in some cases. When they ran a much larger, Llama 70B model their steering overhead increased to only 6%. Not surprisingly, MIA won out over methods that relied on turning off vLLM’s graph replay feature to enable runtime monitoring and steering. It significantly outperformed both the first version of vLLM-Hook and vLLM-Lens , a plugin developed by the UK government that also uses Python hooks to interact with model layers. MIA even outperformed EasySteer , a steering method that ‘forks’ vLLM to add changes to a server-side copy of the official GitHub repo. Forking leaves graph replay on but requires developers to constantly sync their repo with vLLM, which the project officially discourages because of its frequent updates. What’s next Tools that can provide real-time insight and control over AI content generation can be a last line of defense for enterprises with a low tolerance for risk. In experiments, IBM researchers showed that vLLM-Hook MIA can enable this extra layer of protection. vLLM-Hook is already deployed in IBM’s Steerability toolkit , which enables developers to quickly design and evaluate steering methods for different use cases. To give the open source community more experience using these tools, researchers at IBM and elsewhere recently announced The Steerability Challenge , a NeurIPS 2026 competition with a workshop to be hosted at NeurIPS Paris. Participants can compete for $25,000 in prizes by composing a set of steering interventions that suppress “dishonest” behavior without degrading a model’s general capabilities. Serving customers quickly is a top concern for enterprises deploying AI, but so are interpretability and control. With vLLM-Hook MIA, fast inferencing and a more transparent, controllable AI can go together.
