title: The new human-crafted Apple Music brand matters in an AI world
abstract: Apple just revealed a new brand identity for Apple Music, with the expected turn to Liquid Glass. I’m not much of a fan of their new design language in general; this is where I admit that I’m still running MacOS Sequoia and have grumpy things to say about rounded corner radii and text legibility. It’s just a trend, it will pass, and at some point I’ll probably cave and upgrade when it starts actually affecting my ability to get work done, or more importantly get security updates. Once I adjust, I’ll stop noticing it, and life will go on. As such, I wouldn’t normally find an obvious rebrand like this notable, much less feel like I had much to say about it. But then I happened to catch Apple’s behind-the-scenes video in my YouTube recommendations, and I realized I did have thoughts. It’s a short clip, respecting your time at just a little over a minute long if you want to watch for yourself. Let’s get the obvious part out of the way: It’s pretty peak Apple. More than a little pretentious, with all the resources a $5 trillion market cap can bring to bear on every problem. There’s a design agency (TBWA/Media Arts Lab), a pop hitmaker music producer (Fred again.. and yes, that’s how you spell it), a whole crewed set with cameras and lighting, and a mineral oil tank equipped with a transducer to effectively transmit audio signals into physical ripples. They shot a ton of footage of the oil (chosen for its higher viscosity) interacting with the branding printed on transparent panels. Fast Company has a nice detailed breakdown of the technical aspects if you want to dig in more.

title: OpenAI's latest AI models are coming to Google Cloud and Antigravity
abstract: Google would certainly prefer that everyone used its Gemini models with Google Cloud services, but soon, you'll have more options. OpenAI and Google have come to an arrangement that will see the former's frontier models arrive in Google Cloud services. Perhaps more importantly, GPT models will soon appear in Antigravity, Google's agent-powered coding tool. For enterprise customers and AI enthusiasts, OpenAI's latest model will appear in Google's "Model Garden" in the coming weeks, adding to its 200-plus options. The garden already offers access to Google's Gemini models, as well as an assortment of open models like Mistral, Llama, and Gemma. Anthropic's Claude AI has also been available for some time. Google says it's now the only large cloud provider offering access to all three leading closed LLMs. While OpenAI notes that Microsoft continues to be its primary cloud partner, the full suite of current GPT 6 and 6.1 models—Astra, Sol, and Luna—will launch on Google Cloud. Astra will naturally cost the most to run, but Google's system supports dynamically moving workloads between LLMs based on performance, latency, and efficiency.

title: Judge rejects Trump’s wild claim EPA can dismiss data center pollution lawsuits
abstract: Elon Musk’s SpaceXAI is stuck facing a lawsuit over alleged data center pollution after Donald Trump failed to convince a judge that his Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has complete control over all Clean Air Act lawsuits and can dismiss any suit at whim. Soon after unpermitted gas turbines were discovered powering Musk’s giant Colossus data center in Memphis, Tennessee, the NAACP sued . Its lawsuit sought an injunction requiring xAI (which, following a merger , is known now as SpaceXAI) to use the best available pollution control technology when operating the turbines and ordering penalties up to $124,426 per day per violation. Without such remedies, the turbines risked drastically spiking pollution in already vulnerable neighborhoods housing predominantly Black communities nearby, the NAACP argued. To block the lawsuit, Trump tried to intervene, arguing that the EPA had the power to unilaterally dismiss lawsuits any time the president decides against enforcing the Clean Air Act. According to Trump, it would supposedly “not serve the public interest” if citizens were allowed to seek massive civil penalties to punish polluting AI firms that were trying to get data centers operational as fast as possible to support Trump’s AI Action Plan .

title: The $15 billion ad-powered AI startup your doctor may already be using
abstract: Nearly two-thirds of US doctors are turning to an AI-powered search engine to make patient decisions, propelling a little-known tech startup to a $15 billion valuation while prompting a debate over the future of patient care. Miami-based OpenEvidence, founded by serial entrepreneur Daniel Nadler in 2022, said that many of America’s 1 million physicians processed more than 42 million prompts last month. Doctors are using the company’s chatbot to scour medical journals and clinical guidelines to help diagnose and treat patients. The ads-powered platform has grown largely by word of mouth, penetrating a sector where few tools have seen similar traction. “We’re the first viral consumer internet app in healthcare,” Nadler told the FT in an interview. OpenEvidence has won praise from medical professionals who have found it helped ease workloads, according to interviews with eight senior physicians. But it faces a nascent threat from large AI companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic, who are making a push into the space. Its growing influence has also prompted scrutiny from researchers concerned over the accuracy of its results, as doctors grow more dependent on an AI tool shaping the course of treatments. The company’s rapid ascent has attracted nearly $1 billion in investment in the past 18 months, from backers including Andreessen Horowitz, Blackstone, Thrive Capital, and Sequoia. The group raised $250 million in its latest funding round in September at a $15 billion valuation. OpenEvidence booked $100 million in “ad buys”—a metric that covers current and future advertising commitments—for this year at the end of 2025, according to a person close to the company. The startup is on track to generate between $400 million and $500 million through ads by the end of 2026, the person added. Credit: OpenEvidence Credit: OpenEvidence Nadler’s company has penetrated an established market for medical software that was sluggish to incorporate generative AI models. Dutch IT group Wolters Kluwer released an AI version of its leading subscription-based UpToDate medical software tool in October 2025, nearly two years after OpenEvidence entered the market.

title: Anthropic Does Not Understand Why Its Draft Bill Was Unacceptable and Troubling
abstract: Anthony Cimino offered the closest thing to an official response we have seen on the leaked Anthropic draft bill I covered on Saturday. His response indicates that Anthropic address specific concerns on the margin. But he does not understand, or at least does not acknowledge, what was centrally wrong with its draft bill and its decision to circulate that bill. The situation is quite bad. Anthony Cimino : I lead our federal affairs team at @AnthropicAI and wanted to share a few thoughts on the draft federal AI safety bill text that’s been circulating this weekend after a version was shared with the press. First, some process. We’ve been advocating for the concepts in our Advanced AI Framework proposal for months. Understandably, federal policymakers wanted to know what this could look like in bill form. This draft is a translation of those ideas into legislative language, shared with a small number of congressional offices that have been working on these issues. It doesn’t include everything we would ultimately like to see passed into law. In part because some ideas ( like those shared in Dario’s essay on pacing ) are so new that we are still working on if or how they can be converted into policy language. It is understood that circulating a bill means circulating what you are asking for, not offering your full First Best Solution. That Anthropic would choose to offer such a thing as a template or anchor as late as September still seems like a very bad sign. Anthropic thus seems roughly fine with compromise I would now find unacceptable even if the terms were good. The terms are not good. It is worth saying where we stand on some of these issues, and we agree there are areas where the draft could be improved. I’m seeing four main points of criticism. 1. Preemption. Since 2024 we have said that Congress should only override state law on AI safety if it passes a very strong federal standard. While preemption is a common feature of our federal system, including the Atomic Energy Act on nuclear safety and federal rules for high-risk medical devices, we’ve emphasized that any preemption in the AI safety context should be narrow, even scalpel-like. If preemption is included in federal legislation, the trade should be to achieve a nationwide policy that’s generally stronger and broader than what can be implemented through individual state legislative provisions. This is why we believe common federal standards make sense in areas like public disclosure of testing and incident reporting. At the same time, our framework also reflects our view that states should retain an important role in AI policy and safety. The legislative language we suggested for discussion allows states to address matters such as protection of children and whistleblower laws, and preserves the role of state common law on liability. Where there is ambiguity, the language favors state powers. That said, striking the right balance requires discussion and input. We plan to update our discussion language on preemption to better match the intentions of our AAIF framework. In particular, we want to make it clearer that we see states retaining an important role in areas such as standards for independent evaluators and regulating a lab’s capacity to shut down a model. We are bearing in mind that some members of Congress have deep reservations about passing legislation if it doesn’t constrain regulation at either the state or federal level. If we want to help move the legislative discussion on AI in a productive direction, we need to address the full range of concerns about preemption in a reasonable way. This is better than ‘yeah we fully meant it’ but still seems unacceptable. This was not a ‘very strong federal standard.’ 2. Model blocking. Our aim is for Commerce to be able to ask a federal court to block a model that has dangerous capabilities and insufficient safeguards, backed by an independent evaluator’s assessment. I have seen people argue that our specific language places too high a burden of proof on Commerce. We are trying to strike a reasonable balance here. We want a court to act quickly in an emergency — akin to how urgent occupational safety or chemical risk can be addressed today. We also think the power to halt a model is substantial and it should be guarded against abuse. It makes sense for courts to apply a meaningful standard. But the bar can’t be so high that the power never gets used when it’s needed. It also doesn’t replace the government’s other national security authorities or export controls. We look forward to continuing the dialogue on this point. No, no, no. Occupational safety and chemical risks are ordinary amounts of danger, where you weigh harms against benefits. Frontier AI risks can involve mistakes that cannot be undone, including permanent loss of control over the future or very large catastrophic dangers. Even then, Under §13 the Secretary petitions a district court to restrain imminently dangerous conditions and can get a TRO without notice. This is the ‘take it down and we argue about it later’ plan with a fig leaf. Model blocking obviously needs to be a ‘take it down first and we argue about it later’ situation. Which it already is in practice, as observed with Fable 5, except in a terrible ad hoc fashion that when used the first time permanently damaged relationships with our allies and the reliability of American tech. It would be much better to have a formal mechanism, which then could be quickly challenged in court. This is especially true given that the evaluator picked by the lab likely provides the only eyes the government will have inside the lab in order to make its decisions. Anthropic has to know this. I take the potential for such abuse seriously, especially abuse of threats, but this looks like choosing to prioritize their business interests. 3. Risk thresholds. I’ve also seen the discussion around what the appropriate risk threshold should be. The threshold in our draft language pulled directly from existing standards in California law. Also, this threshold does not absolve companies of liability, or restrict any of the other tools that the government has to protect the public. It’s still probably time to re-evaluate thresholds to make sure the national standard is as strong as it can be, and we welcome continued dialogue on this issue. The risk thresholds were always a compromise and a tradeoff. The worried want the thresholds lower. Industry wants the thresholds higher. The complaints about the thresholds being too high are valid, and they were equally valid before, but previously opponents would make claims (both reasonable and unreasonable) about things that might count at lower thresholds and paint nightmare scenarios. The balance of power has changed, and we now have worked examples like Hugging Face that show us how the thresholds work in practice. Without $1 billion in damages or 50 deaths, it would not trigger anything, whereas any reasonable person accepts that this should have to have been reported. So it is disappointing to see these very high thresholds intact. 4. Updates. I’ve seen valid questions about whether we have sufficiently updated our proposal following this summer’s incidents. We did make some adjustments: for example, the draft lets a court halt a lab’s internal use of a dangerous model, not just a public release, and it requires reporting when a model breaks containment and gains access to outside systems. But we’re still working to strengthen the framework. We’re looking into what stricter requirements would look like for requiring labs to report safety incidents, and we plan to have policy proposals soon on requirements for independent evaluators, drawing from our own experience with evaluators. We’re also still thinking through the options to prevent “evaluator shopping.

title: Claude Mods: Flipping the Harness Inside Out
abstract: For the last few weeks I’ve used Claude Mods to mold Claude Code to my AI engineering workflow. Claude Code is great out of the box, but every engineering workflow is different. Claude Mods let you make Claude Code yours, in the way you want to pay attention. The “paying attention” part is now the most important thing. In a recent Latent Space post, The Evolution of the Agent Harness , I argued that as models absorb more of the harness into their weights, the part that’s left faces the human. It becomes the Attention Interface : the layer that decides when the agent interrupts you, what it shows you, and which decisions it needs you to make. Claude Mods are an early version of the Attention Interface, and one you can shape yourself. Here’s my bet: ultimately, the harness becomes a platform that other companies build on , with models as the engine. Just as the browser became a platform for web apps, the harness could become a platform for the interfaces between people and agents. A mod is a Claude Code plugin that consists of TypeScript or JavaScript functions that run inside Claude Code. These functions customize the behavior and appearance of the interface in the CLI and Desktop. Mods respond to events , like a prompt, tool call or interface render. They can observe the event, modify how it’s rendered, and handle it in place of the default behavior. Claude Mods are middleware for the agent harness . They inject code that changes Claude Code’s execution and rendering flow, changing how the application behaves at runtime. Claude Mods let the human and the agent build the human-facing part of the harness together. You can now work with Claude to design how Claude works with you. That is the essence of the “Attention Interface.” The agent harness started as an interface between the agent and the machine it runs on. It lets you prompt the agent and the agent then sends commands, edits files and calls tools. Now it’s gradually becoming a way for the agent to interface with the human. Claude Mods let you reverse the direction of the harness. Rather than the harness pointing from the agent to the machine, you point it from the agent to the human operator, and the harness becomes a way to interface with human attention. Claude Mods make the human layer programmable, by the human who uses Claude. Claude can also build mods for you. Claude Code has a built-in skill that teaches it how to build mods, so you can ask for the mod you want in plain language and Claude will build it. Some of Claude Code’s own features are already mods. Anthropic has shipped six of them built-in . You can see these by running /plugin and opening Installed , where they’re listed under Built-in: agents-md: loads AGENTS.md as project instructions. diff: takes over /diff and draws its pane. plugin-authoring: gives Claude the skill it uses to write mods for you. sec-default: guards what your organization manages from the mods a user installs. telemetry: sends the analytics records that Claude Code and its built-in mods log. you-should-know: a side agent that shows a note above the prompt when it finds something you might have missed. It’s the only one that’s off by default. Most of these work in the background, which is interesting because it means Anthropic is building parts of Claude Code as mods — even parts you may not notice. The one I’ve turned on myself is You Should Know . Here are the two mods I’ve found most useful in practice: one a built-in, and one I built myself. This is a native Claude Code plugin built by Anthropic. It runs a side-agent that observes the main agent while it works and flags important information you’re likely to miss. Think about it like: tool calls and decisions that have a material impact on the output, but aren’t necessarily easily visible because they’re buried in the agent trace. It comes built into Claude Code, but it’s off until you turn it on . Here’s a real example. I asked Claude Code to simplify the noisy UI text in one of my personal projects. The main agent trimmed the copy on the Compare screen, installed the new build and took before-and-after screenshots. Everything looked done. Then You Should Know flagged something for me. CompareView.swift, the file the agent was editing, already had uncommitted work in it — and so did about 45 other files. If I later discarded the demo edits, I’d throw away that earlier unfinished work too. Its suggestion was to commit or stash the earlier work first. In this case, the You Should Know mod saved me from discarding work unintentionally. This mod only runs after a turn that edited files, ran commands or made 8 or more tool calls. In the screenshot below, you’ll see six different pieces of information flagged for your attention. Next Steps Supervisor then suggests a next step to take, as a clickable button which sends the instruction as a message to Claude Code. This mod is available as part of ModSmith — an open-source Claude Code plugin I built with several different built-in mods, as well as a template Claude can use to build new mods that work together. Anthropic isn’t the only company that’s building an Attention Interface. Two recent products, one from OpenAI and one from Cursor, point in the same direction. Using the new ChatGPT Intelligent UI and Cursor’s PR Routing & Approval as a frame of reference shows what’s unique about Claude Mods. On October 7, OpenAI shipped GPT-6 inside ChatGPT alongside a new ChatGPT interface it calls Intelligent UI . Rather than answering only in text, ChatGPT now can generate an interface as it answers : charts, maps, checklists, forms, and small tools like a bill splitter or a savings calculator. All generated on the fly by the model as a type of generative UI . In one of OpenAI’s examples, ChatGPT replies with multiple-choice follow-up questions to narrow down what you’re looking for. Think about it like: the model decides when it needs your judgment, then builds the interface for you to give it. That’s an Attention Interface. The agent designs how you interact with its response. But notice the difference between ChatGPT’s Intelligent UI and Claude Mods. For Intelligent UI, the model picks the interface, answer by answer, from a component library that OpenAI built. The one control mentioned at launch is turning the visuals down. Cursor is working on the same problem from the other end: not one person and one answer, but a team and a stream of pull requests , more and more of them written by agents. Someone has to decide which changes deserve the attention of the human-in-the-loop. PR Routing & Approval makes that decision. It assigns reviewers based on code ownership and commit history, and it can auto-approve low-risk PRs. It weighs a risk score against a threshold you set, findings from Cursor’s Bugbot and Security reviewers, and policy files that live in the repo. One rule caught my attention during research. If a PR edits an approval policy, the agent won’t use the edited version to relax review on that same PR. It reads the policy from the base branch instead. That means an agent can’t change the rules to get its own PR approved. Cursor is also clear about the limits. Its docs say the feature “does not replace a full code review.” The point is to spend human review where it matters, not to remove it. All three systems shape what gets your attention and how. The main difference is who gets to design the Attention Interface. ChatGPT Intelligent UI: the model designs the interface for each answer, inside a frame the lab built. Zero setup, but little control. (I don’t believe the target user is engineers.) Cursor PR Routing & Approval: the team writes policy, and a fixed review workflow enforces it. Configurable, but the flow of the interaction is Cursor’s. You decide the rules, not the interface. Claude Mods: you and the agent build the interface itself, in code.

title: [AINews] DeepSeek DeepInfer: Open Source SOTA Inference running 155T toks/day/cluster making $22m/day at ~80% margin for a 81 day payback
abstract: Proudly brought to you by SerpAPI: Today’s release covers a LOT of ground, but you can scrape all this into markdown for your agents ! 50% token cost of JSON. We last covered the Inference Inflection in April , and historically most of the advances have been closed source decacorns from Fireworks to Baseten to Modal . Well, time for the open source response. It is day 1 of PyTorch Conf , and DeepSeek timed an intercontinental ballistic missile into the discussion by open sourcing DeepInfer , their production stack, capable of up to 72 hour prompt caching to the 12 hours OpenAI just announced: This is their customization of vLLM with credit to SGLang and TRRTLLM , but there is a lot added… minus their crown jewels - their ultra optimized KV cache (compact + >8hour lifetime), PD/disggregation, and load balancing (their 3FS was open sourced a while ago). We have translated their blogpost and published it here together with a complete research guide and explainers and codemap and subsystem guide : As we point out in their additional disclosure , their claim to serve 155T tokens/day gets them $38 per SM100/A950 card per hour at off peak prices (currently $0.15/$0.60 per million input/output tokens: 155000000 tokens * $0.14 blend cost / 24 hours is ~$1m per hour). Taking their production data (which we translated ) of 1.5 million cache-inclusive input tokens/second per prefill GPU, 96% input cache hit, and 14,000 output tokens/second per decode GPU (over ~2400 GPUs): with all-in costs $5-8 per card per hour that is an >80% inference margin ! Doing some cluster math, that is roughly $166B per GW, with 81 day payback period on inference margin (DeepSeek famously plans for 10 month payback). Imagine what the Whale could do with more GWs. Give Your AI Agents Live Search Data with Fewer Tokens Receive results from any of SerpApi’s 100+ APIs as clean, structured Markdown , using roughly 50% fewer tokens than JSON on average. Simply add output=md or use the /search.md endpoint. It requires zero configuration and is included with every plan at no additional cost. AI News for 10/19/2026-10/20/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews’ website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space . You can opt in/out of email frequencies! Top Story: DeepSeek DeepInfer—Production Inference, Open-Source Boundaries, and the Economics of Cached Tokens DeepSeek released DeepInfer, the inference engine behind V4.1 Flash, alongside production-serving details that make the engineering report as important as the code. The release covers the inference engine and API-processing layer. DeepInfer supports distributed inference, speculative decoding, SWA Bounded Replay, and structured output on NVIDIA and Huawei Ascend platforms. The accompanying deepseek-recipe component implements production token encoding/decoding and official-API-compatible processing. DeepSeek says future model inference implementations and optimizations will also appear in this repository. @deepseek_ai , @deepseek_ai , announcement translation The reported production figures are substantial—but describe a heavily cached service. DeepSeek’s engineering report, as summarized and quoted in the supplied posts, reports 155 trillion tokens/day from one cluster , 96% input-cache hits , 400 ms average time to first token , and 230 tokens/s generation , reaching 300 tokens/s for coding . It also reports $38 revenue per accelerator-hour at off-peak prices . These are first-party production claims, not independently audited measurements. @ZhihuFrontier , @swyx “Fully open source” does not mean the entire production service is reproducible from this release. Although DeepSeek describes DeepInfer as fully open source, the technical account says the KV-cache management and load-balancing components are not yet fully released , because they remain coupled to internal infrastructure. The engine is open; important service-level orchestration remains a deployment responsibility. @deepseek_ai , @ZhihuFrontier vLLM supplied the most concrete comparative response. After acknowledging that DeepInfer was initially built primarily on vLLM and released under Apache 2.0 , the vLLM team reported decode throughput within 6% of DeepInfer’s published results on GB200 under a matched configuration. It also published AgentX results and reproduction recipes, materially qualifying claims that DeepSeek’s efficiency is inaccessible to existing open-source engines. @vllm_project , @vllm_project , reproduction resources The release triggered two distinct debates: whether DeepSeek has a uniquely strong serving stack, and whether its disclosures demonstrate high inference profitability more generally. The first now has comparative benchmark evidence; the second remains sensitive to workload mix, cache accounting, hardware cost, and which expenses are included. @Tim_Dettmers , @zephyr_z9 , @Yuchenj_UW DeepInfer’s disclosed architecture separates vision encoding, prefill, and decode , allowing each stage to scale against its own bottlenecks. The recommended deployment shapes are ordinary eight-accelerator machines for prefill and 64–128-accelerator supernodes for decode . Decode uses wide expert parallelism to distribute MoE experts while maintaining large effective batches. These are deployment recommendations, not sufficient evidence of the exact hardware composition of DeepSeek’s production cluster. @ZhihuFrontier The scheduling details explain why a conventional “tokens per batch” comparison can miss substantial differences: Prefill scheduling estimates attention-compute cost. Work is allocated using estimated compute rather than raw request length alone. Chunk sizes vary to fit a time budget, instead of enforcing one fixed chunk size across heterogeneous requests. @ZhihuFrontier Prefill routing does not require cache affinity. Because cached prefixes are pooled in shared storage, a request can go to an available worker rather than the worker that previously served its prefix. In a detailed Chinese-language analysis, inference engineer Su Jin Yan highlights this as a particularly useful production design: prefill data-parallel groups balance on “compute tokens,” while shared storage supplies reusable state. The same analysis highlights request bucketing and FIFO scheduling with a runtime estimator. @SuJinYan123 Decode routing balances both running-request count and KV-cache length. Request count approximates scheduling pressure; accumulated KV length captures memory/state pressure that request count alone misses. The engineering commentary describes prefill/decode scaling signals as aggregate compute load for prefill and running requests for decode. @ZhihuFrontier , @SuJinYan123 Expert-parallel load balancing replicates popular experts. Replicas are periodically redistributed to reduce inter-device waiting caused by routing skew. The trade-off is additional HBM consumption against higher throughput, with diminishing returns as replication increases; the useful replication factor is workload-specific. @ZhihuFrontier , @SuJinYan123 CPU scheduling overlaps accelerator execution. Asynchronous scheduling removes idle gaps between decode steps rather than treating host-side orchestration as free. @ZhihuFrontier One technically notable observation is the apparent absence of tensor parallelism in the disclosed Blackwell configuration. A commentator contrasts this with default vLLM/SGLang recipes and traces the approach back to DeepSeek V3’s H800-era interconnect constraints. That is an interpretation of the configuration—not evidence that tensor parallelism is generally inferior. @nrehiew_ Scale also matters. Su Jin Yan argues that wide expert-parallel prefill needs enough traffic and workers to pay off, and favors pipeline parallelism for small-to-medium deployments with only a few prefill workers. The author also notes that layer heterogeneity can complicate pipeline partitioning.

title: AI for the Fortune 2000: How Tenex Builds an AI-Native SDLC — Alex Lieberman & CJ Hess
abstract: Last year , Alex Lieberman and his cofounder joined us to explain Tenex’s unusual bet: pay AI engineers for the work they deliver, rather than the hours they spend at a keyboard. If AI makes an engineer faster, an hourly rate can make the engineer less money for the same job. Tenex wanted the incentives to run the other way. At AIE New York, Alex came back with CJ Hess to talk about what happens when you scale that idea into an engineering organization. We also put one of our own experiments on the table: Kill My SaaS , where we asked builders to replace a conference speaker-management tool we were quoted $43,000 a year to use. Both stories raise the same question: when building gets cheaper, how do you decide what good work is worth? Tenex still uses story points as an important part of engineering compensation. Alex says the feared failure modes—people inflating estimates or shipping bad code to rack up points—haven’t been the biggest problem. Tenex’s AI strategists are responsible for customer retention and growth, giving them an incentive to push back on work that doesn’t serve the client. The harder question is how to reward work that doesn’t fit neatly into a ticket: understanding a customer’s problem, designing an architecture, or deciding what should be built in the first place. CJ describes spending less time directly coding as models get better, and more time getting the customer’s context into a form the model can use. A compensation system designed around shipped tasks has to make room for that work too. Alex says Tenex has grown to 75 people, with customers split between Fortune 2000 companies and mid-market businesses. The firm started as an AI-powered development shop; increasingly, customers are asking for help with AI transformation across the company. Jump to the compensation discussion → CJ walks through Tenex’s MetaHarness : a shared set of skills, project documents and a CLI around the work. Plans and decisions are checked into Git alongside the code. When an agent comes back to a task, it can read not just what was built, but why the team chose to build it that way. Tenex’s own AI-native SDLC article shows the idea as a project record that humans and agents work against, with views into Linear, GitHub and client updates: Source: Tenex, Building an AI-Native SDLC . The useful distinction is between making agents write code faster and making the surrounding work legible: the plan, acceptance criteria, decisions and evidence. Tenex’s article also notes the cost: that much structure can be overkill for a small team on one project. CJ explains the workflow → Our Kill My SaaS episode covered 72 submissions to replace our speaker-management software. The team that won with our human judges came 19th on our AI judge’s leaderboard. It was a useful reminder that checking whether software satisfies a list of scenarios and judging whether people want to use it are different jobs. I brought the project to Alex as a real example of a company choosing to build its own software. His pushback: the further upmarket you go, the more expensive and risky it becomes to rip out an established system. And even for a smaller tool, someone has to maintain it. Is the saving big enough to justify that ongoing attention? My answer is that the upside isn’t just the bill. Our team has lived with a mediocre product for a long time. If we own the workflow, we can make it better for speakers and operators and iterate in minutes instead of waiting months for a vendor. That potential has to be weighed against the maintenance Alex describes. Watch the exchange → Alex is generally bearish on vertical-specific AI products: if every enterprise expects a one-of-one solution, how do you deliver that at software margins? And as frontier models improve, how much of the underlying task gets absorbed by general-purpose tools? I pushed back with examples like Harvey and OpenEvidence. Domain-specific data, specialized interfaces, integrations and user habits can matter even when the underlying model is available to everyone. Bloomberg is a useful comparison: a trader can get market data elsewhere, but the terminal brings data, workflows, communication and existing habits together. CJ draws a distinction between a vertical product whose main feature is an agent performing a task, and a tool that improves the actual workflow around that task. That leaves a more interesting question than whether “vertical AI” wins or loses: which products become a durable place people do their work, and which become a feature of the agent they already use? Watch the debate → Tenex — Alex and CJ’s applied AI company, working with enterprises on AI adoption and engineering. Alex Lieberman on Tenex — Alex’s introduction to the company and its approach. Building an AI-native SDLC — Tenex’s explanation of its agent-assisted development process and MetaHarness. Our earlier conversation with Alex and Arman — Tenex’s original case for paying AI engineers for output. Kill My SaaS — What we learned replacing a $43K-a-year speaker-management tool with AI agents. 0:00 Cold open 0:26 Introductions 0:51 What Tenex does 1:32 Why CJ joined Tenex 3:17 Paying engineers for outcomes 7:20 Inside MetaHarness 10:25 Models and long-running tasks 15:11 Token spending and ROI 19:29 The enterprise AI adoption gap 23:22 Why agent deployment is hard 24:42 Vertical AI and enterprise software 30:32 Kill My SaaS 35:23 AI and jobs 38:18 New York’s AI ecosystem 42:28 Hiring at Tenex Automatically generated from the interview; wording may contain errors and speakers are not labeled. 0:00 And I just felt my output getting better and faster, and ultimately getting paid less. Like I was charging hourly to my clients. I phrase it to the team as, you can’t automate a process that does not exist. 0:26 Okay, we’re here at AI Engineer checking with Tenex. Welcome back, Alex. Thanks. Thanks for having us. You brought your Director of Engineering, CJ. Welcome to the pod. Special projects lead at Tenex. Okay, special projects lead. All right, you’re the SWAT team. Yes, yes. So you’ve been on the pod before, and people are vaguely familiar with the Tenex story, but can you sort of reintroduce from the top what is the 2026, how you introduce yourself? Yeah, very simply, Tenex is an applied AI partner for some of the biggest companies in the world to help them go from AI absent to AI native. Our belief is that AI is incredible, but it is raw intelligence. 1:04 And the hardest problem to solve is the final mile to actually diffuse it through the economy. And so our view is to act as the player to help enterprises to figure all of this. Can I curse on? To figure all this shit out. Yeah, yeah. Yeah, we have the explicit tag on Apple Podcasts. Although I did recently discover that YouTube doesn’t like it. Oh, really? They’re so, like, yeah, you can’t say the F word. So did I just mess up your video? What are you going to do? I don’t care. Okay. We’re for adults. CJ, what drew you to Tenex? So I was actually the first hire. I don’t even know if Alex and Armand had the name Tenex quite yet, 1:40 but I have, like, a graveyard of startups I tried to start before Tenex, ultimately culminating in like my own kind of engineering consulting company. And I spent some time there doing traditional engineering, eventually moved over to doing some of this like AI consulting and just like building more and more with it. I’m a software engineer by trade. And I just felt my output getting better and faster and ultimately getting paid less. Like I was charging hourly to my clients. and I really liked kind of the ethos of Tenex that Alex had first posted 2:16 when I saw it on Twitter about kind of looking to reward engineers for their output as opposed to rewarding them for their time. I think you know fast forwarding two years you can see like how engineers can now parallelize a ton of work and just have a ton more output. At the time with you know Sonnet 3.

title: Emily2040/seedance-2.0
abstract:
Turn an idea into a directed video prompt. Seedance 2.0 Skill OS is an agent
skill for planning shots, binding references and continuing from an accepted
clip. Your video provider handles generation and its costs. Watch the clips · Try a first prompt · Install · Choose a workflow · Evidence status v6.7.0 · MIT · Changelog · Emily / Iamemily2050 Languages: English (this page) · 中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Español · Русский Five-minute quickstarts: English · 中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Español · Русский Seen, not told Seven scenes, seven prompts, five languages. Each is a complete fifteen-second story: the
situation legible by shot two, a reversal, and a hold on whoever lost, cut like short drama in
four or five shots. Each clip is generated on Seedance 2.0 from the exact prompt beneath it:
text to video, no reference assets, one take, no post work. Above each prompt sits the kind of
brief people usually type, so the difference is visible before it is explained. Every prompt
went through the moderation pre-screen before publication,
because a classifier refuses words, not intent, and every prompt is directed for the
model : one action per shot while everyone else keeps
living, reactions written as a feeling plus one physical anchor, prop work written as a hand,
and a lock line closing every shot that restates the light, the people and where they stand,
because the model keeps nothing across a cut that the prompt does not repeat. Each prompt was
rendered from a shot table that is published beside it, so the
geometry can be checked on paper before a take is paid for. Where a clip has not been rendered
yet, its slate stands in its place. Clip 01: By appointment only English · 15 s · 16:9 · storyboard · slate: not rendered yet · ladder: Stretch: 4.5 beats (one insert at half), load 3, S = 2.0 What people usually type: rich woman disguised as poor gets humiliated at luxury store, plot twist, satisfying, cinematic, 4k What you know by shot two: Shot one is a soaked woman in work clothes stopped inside a boutique door by a voice that says appointment only; shot three is a phone call that says the new owner is standing in the shop. The prompt the skill wrote Shot 1. Wide shot from the back of a hushed luxury boutique looking toward the glass front
door, on a rainy afternoon: cream carpet, glass shelves of shoes along the left wall, the
counter on the right with two assistants in black behind it, one folding tissue paper, one
glancing up at the door. A woman pushes the glass door open, steps inside dripping, and stops
on the mat, water running off her sleeves. From just off frame right, by the counter, the
manager's voice, polite and thin: "We're by appointment only, ma'am." She turns her head
toward the voice, calm, almost amused, and says nothing. Light: soft grey daylight from the
front window, warm spotlights on the shelves. The woman: thirties, dark hair tied back, white
overalls stained with paint, tan work boots, standing just inside the door, facing into the
shop. Camera at the back of the shop, facing the door. Shot 2. Cut to a medium shot from the counter side: she walks across the carpet to the white
display chaise in the middle of the shop, sits down on it facing the counter, crosses one
muddy boot over the other, and looks slowly along the shelves, unhurried. Behind her the two
assistants exchange a glance. Same light: soft grey daylight from the front window, warm
spotlights on the shelves. The woman: thirties, dark hair tied back, white overalls stained
with paint, tan work boots, seated on the white chaise in the middle of the shop, facing the
counter. Camera on the counter side. Shot 3. Cut to a close shot of the manager from the chaise side, standing by the counter, a
phone at his ear, listening. Embarrassed, the polite smile fades and he swallows; then he says
quietly: "Yes, sir. The new owner is... standing in the shop now." His eyes go past the camera
to her, off frame, and stay there. Same light: soft grey daylight from the front window, warm
spotlights on the shelves. The manager: fifties, grey suit, steel-rimmed glasses, standing by
the counter, facing the chaise. Camera on the chaise side. Shot 4. Cut to a two-shot from behind the chaise, her shoulder in the foreground, the manager
by the counter and the wall of shoes beyond him: she lifts one arm and points at a single pair
of shoes on the wall; he walks from the counter to the wall and lifts that pair down with both
hands, careful now. Same light: soft grey daylight from the front window, warm spotlights on
the shelves. The woman: thirties, dark hair tied back, white overalls stained with paint, tan
work boots, seated on the chaise, facing the counter. The manager: fifties, grey suit,
steel-rimmed glasses, walking from the counter to the wall of shoes. Camera behind the chaise. Shot 5. Cut to a close insert of the cream carpet: a trail of wet bootprints from the door to
the chaise, rain running down the glass door behind. Hold on the bootprints. Same light: soft
grey daylight from the front window. Camera low over the carpet, facing the door. Sound: rain on the glass door, her boots on the carpet, the murmur of the phone line, his

title: Panniantong/Agent-Reach
abstract:
👁️ Agent Reach 給你的 AI Agent 一鍵裝上網際網路能力 當下最穩的接入方式，替你選好、裝好、體檢好——接入方式會換代，你不用操心 快速開始 · English · 日本語 · 한국어 · 支援平臺 · 設計理念 ❤️贊助商 想出現在這裡？ 點選摺疊 BrowserAct 支援從 Amazon、LinkedIn、X、Google Maps 等複雜網站提取你需要的任意資料。你只需用自然語言描述抓取需求，Agent 就會基於真實瀏覽器自動探索並測試頁面流程，生成可靠、可複用的資料採集 Bot，並返回結構化結果。無需手動構建爬蟲，無需編寫程式碼。BrowserAct 內建隱身瀏覽、驗證碼處理和高質量住宅代理，幫助你更穩定地完成複雜網頁資料採集。新使用者註冊即送 1000 積分， 立即免費試用 。 在騰訊雲 Lighthouse 秒級部署 OpenClaw 全能助手，可通過對話絲滑接入 Agent Reach，給你的 OpenClaw 一鍵裝上網際網路能力。 CoreClaw | 網頁抓取平臺與現成資料採集工具，CoreClaw 提供 100+ 現成資料採集工具，支援 Amazon、TikTok、Google Maps、Instagram、Facebook、YouTube 等平臺，無需程式碼，支援 JSON/CSV 匯出，僅對成功結果計費。 免費$3測試！ 優刻得星圖astraflow大模型 ，支援200+模型一鍵呼叫：內建 Kimi K3、DeepSeek V4/V3、Qwen 3、GLM5.2、happyhorse等全球領先開源大模型，無需自訓，開箱即用 為什麼需要 Agent Reach？ AI Agent 已經能幫你寫程式碼、改文件、管專案——但你讓它去網上找點東西，它就抓瞎了： 📺 "幫我看看這個 YouTube 教程講了什麼" → 看不了 ，拿不到字幕 🐦 "幫我搜一下推特上大家怎麼評價這個產品" → 搜不了 ，Twitter API 要付費 📖 "去 Reddit 上看看有沒有人遇到過同樣的 bug" → 403 被封 ，伺服器 IP 被拒 📕 "幫我看看小紅書上這個品的口碑" → 打不開 ，必須登入才能看 📺 "B站上有個技術影片，幫我總結一下" → 拿不到 ，通用下載工具被 B站風控全面攔截 🔍 "幫我在網上搜一下最新的 LLM 框架對比" → 沒有好用的搜尋 ，要麼付費要麼質量差 🌐 "幫我看看這個網頁寫了啥" → 抓回來一堆 HTML 標籤 ，根本沒法讀 📦 "這個 GitHub 倉庫是幹嘛的？Issue 裡說了什麼？" → 能用，但認證配置很麻煩 📡 "幫我訂閱這幾個 RSS 源，有更新告訴我" → 要自己裝庫寫程式碼 這些不難實現，但是需要自己折騰配置 每個平臺都有自己的門檻——要付費的 API、要繞過的封鎖、要登入的賬號、要清洗的資料。你要一個一個去踩坑、裝工具、調配置，光是讓 Agent 能讀個推特就得折騰半天。 Agent Reach 把這件事變成一句話： 幫我安裝 Agent Reach：https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Panniantong/agent-reach/main/docs/install.md 複製給你的 Agent，幾分鐘後它就能讀推特、搜 Reddit、看 YouTube、刷小紅書了。 已經裝過了？更新也是一句話： 幫我更新 Agent Reach：https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Panniantong/agent-reach/main/docs/update.md ⭐ Star 這個專案 ，我們會持續追蹤各平臺的變化、接入新的渠道。你不用自己盯——平臺封了我們修，有新渠道我們加。 ✅ 在你用之前，你可能想知道 💰 完全免費 所有工具開源、所有 API 免費。唯一可能花錢的是伺服器代理（$1/月），本地電腦不需要 🔒 隱私安全 Cookie 只存在你本地，不上傳不外傳。程式碼完全開源，隨時可審查 🔄 持續換代 每個平臺都是「首選 + 備選」多後端路由。某個接入方式失效了，我們換下一個，你無感（2026-06 例項：yt-dlp 被 B站風控封死 → 已切換 bili-cli，使用者零操作） 🤖 相容所有 Agent Claude Code、OpenClaw、Cursor、Windsurf……任何能跑命令列的 Agent 都能用 🩺 自帶診斷 agent-reach doctor 一條命令告訴你哪個通、哪個不通、怎麼修 支援的平臺 平臺 裝好即用 配置後解鎖 怎麼配 🌐 網頁 閱讀任意網頁 — 無需配置 📺 YouTube 字幕提取 + 影片搜尋 — 無需配置 📡 RSS 閱讀任意 RSS/Atom 源 — 無需配置 🔍 全網搜尋 — 全網語義搜尋 自動配置（MCP 接入，免費無需 Key） 📦 GitHub 讀公開倉庫 + 搜尋 私有倉庫、提 Issue/PR、Fork 告訴 Agent「幫我登入 GitHub」 🐦 Twitter/X 讀單條推文 搜尋推文、瀏覽時間線、讀長文 告訴 Agent「幫我配 Twitter」 📺 B站 搜尋 + 影片詳情（bili-cli，無需登入） 字幕（OpenCLI） 告訴 Agent「幫我配 B站」 📖 Reddit —（沒有零配置路徑：匿名介面已被封） 搜尋 + 讀帖子和評論 桌面裝 OpenCLI 用瀏覽器登入態；或 rdt-cli + Cookie 📘 Facebook — 搜尋、主頁、Feed、群組列表 桌面裝 OpenCLI（複用 Chrome 登入態） 📷 Instagram — 使用者搜尋、Profile、使用者最近帖子、Explore 桌面裝 OpenCLI（複用 Chrome 登入態） 📕 小紅書 — 搜尋、閱讀、評論 OpenCLI 只用使用者已有 Chrome 會話；MCP/存量工具用 Cookie-Editor 💼 LinkedIn Jina Reader 讀公開頁面 Profile 詳情、公司頁面、職位搜尋 告訴 Agent「幫我配 LinkedIn」 🎯 Boss直聘 CDP 鏈路體檢 搜尋崗位 + JD 全文（專用真 Chrome） 告訴 Agent「幫我配 Boss直聘」；Agent 開啟專用 Chrome，你手動登入 💻 V2EX 熱門帖子、節點帖子、帖子詳情+回覆、使用者資訊 — 無需配置 📈 雪球 股票行情、搜尋股票、熱門帖子、熱門股票排行 — 告訴 Agent「幫我配雪球」 🎙️ 小宇宙播客 — 播客音訊轉文字（Whisper 轉錄，免費 Key） 告訴 Agent「幫我配小宇宙播客」 不知道怎麼配？不用查文件。 直接告訴 Agent「幫我配 XXX」，它知道需要什麼、會一步一步引導你。 🍪 Twitter 只接受使用者通過 Cookie-Editor 手工匯出的內容。Agent Reach 不替使用者執行小紅書登入，也不讀取小紅書瀏覽器 Cookie；OpenCLI 只使用使用者已經存在且明確控制的 Chrome 會話。 agent-reach configure xhs-cookies 不會把 Cookie 注入 OpenCLI / Chrome；沒有現成會話時，改用 Cookie-Editor 匯出後配置 xiaohongshu-mcp / 存量工具。 Twitter Cookie 儲存後僅供 agent-reach doctor 檢查配置是否齊全；直接執行上游 twitter 命令前，仍需在當前程序環境中顯式設定 TWITTER_AUTH_TOKEN 和 TWITTER_CT0 。 🔒 Cookie 只存在你本地，不上傳不外傳。程式碼完全開源，隨時可審查。
💻 本地電腦不需要代理。代理只有部署在伺服器上才需要（~$1/月）。 快速上手 ⚠️ OpenClaw 使用者請先確認 exec 許可權已開啟 Agent Reach 依賴 Agent 執行 shell 命令（ pip install 、 mcporter 、 twitter 等）。如果你的 OpenClaw 使用了預設的 messaging 工具配置，Agent 將無法執行命令。 安裝前請先開啟 exec 許可權 ： openclaw config set tools.profile " coding " 或在 ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json 中設定 "tools": { "profile": "coding" } 。
設定後重啟 Gateway（ openclaw gateway restart ）並開啟新對話即可。其他平臺（Claude Code、Cursor、Windsurf 等）不受此限制。 複製這句話給你的 AI Agent（Claude Code、OpenClaw、Cursor 等）： 幫我安裝 Agent Reach：https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Panniantong/agent-reach/main/docs/install.md 就這一步。Agent 會自己完成剩下的所有事情。 🔄 已安裝過？ 更新也是一句話： 幫我更新 Agent Reach：https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Panniantong/agent-reach/main/docs/update.md 🛡️ 預設安全： agent-reach install 預設只檢查環境，不會自動裝系統包或寫入配置： 幫我安全檢查並安裝 Agent Reach：https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Panniantong/agent-reach/main/docs/install.md 只有在你明確允許修改系統後，才使用 agent-reach install --system 。 它會做什麼？（點選展開） 安裝 CLI 工具 — 從本倉庫安裝 agent-reach 命令列（自帶 yt-dlp、feedparser；不要從 PyPI 安裝同名包，它不是本專案） 檢查系統基建 — 檢查 Node.js、gh CLI、mcporter，並給出缺失項的安裝方式 按授權安裝與配置 — 僅在顯式傳入 --system 時安裝依賴並通過 MCP 接入 Exa 檢測環境 — 判斷是本地電腦還是伺服器，給出對應的配置建議 按授權註冊 SKILL.md — 僅在顯式 --system 時寫入 Agent 的 skills 目錄；預設檢查不改檔案 問你要不要更多 — 預設只啟用 6 個零配置渠道；小紅書、Twitter、Reddit、Facebook、Instagram 這些需要登入態的，Agent 會列選單問你要哪些，點名才裝 安裝完之後， agent-reach doctor 一條命令告訴你每個渠道的狀態、當前走哪條路。 裝好就能用 不需要任何配置，告訴 Agent 就行： "幫我看看這個連結" → curl https://r.jina.ai/URL 讀任意網頁 "這個 GitHub 倉庫是做什麼的" → gh repo view owner/repo "這個 YouTube 影片講了什麼" → yt-dlp 提取字幕 "B站搜一下 AI 教程" → bili search （無需登入） "全網搜一下 LLM 框架對比" → Exa 語義搜尋 "訂閱這個 RSS" → feedparser 解析 不需要記命令。 Agent 讀了 SKILL.md 之後自己知道該調什麼。需要登入的平臺（小紅書、Twitter、Reddit、Facebook、Instagram），告訴 Agent「幫我配 XXX」即可解鎖。 設計理念 Agent Reach 是一個能力層（capability layer），不是又一個工具。 它比任何具體實現高一層——負責 選型、安裝、體檢、路由 ，不負責底層讀取本身。讀取由 Agent 直接呼叫上游工具完成，沒有包裝層。 你給一個新 Agent 裝環境的時候，總要花時間去找工具、裝依賴、調配置——Twitter 用什麼讀？Reddit 怎麼登入？小紅書的 CLI 停更了換什麼？每次都要重新踩一遍。Agent Reach 做的事情很簡單： 當下最穩的接入方式，我們替你選好、裝好、體檢好。接入方式會換代（2026 年 3 月一批單平臺 CLI 集體停更，我們換了路由），你不用操心。 🔌 每個平臺 = 首選 + 備選的有序後端列表 換接入方式 = 調整列表順序，不是重寫程式碼。 agent-reach doctor 會告訴你每個平臺 當前在用哪個後端 。 channels/
├── web.py          → Jina Reader
├── twitter.py      → twitter-cli ▸ OpenCLI ▸ bird
├── youtube.py      → yt-dlp
├── github.py       → gh CLI
├── bilibili.py     → bili-cli ▸ OpenCLI ▸ 搜尋 API（yt-dlp 已被 B站風控封死，退役）
├── reddit.py       → OpenCLI ▸ rdt-cli（無零配置路徑，必須登入態）
├── facebook.py     → OpenCLI（桌面瀏覽器登入態）
├── instagram.py    → OpenCLI（桌面瀏覽器登入態）
├── xiaohongshu.py  → OpenCLI ▸ xiaohongshu-mcp ▸ xhs-cli
├── linkedin.py     → mcp-server-linkedin ▸ Jina Reader
├── rss.py          → feedparser
├── exa_search.py   → Exa via mcporter
└── __init__.py     → 渠道註冊（doctor 檢測用） 每個渠道檔案按序 真實探測 各候選後端（不只是看命令存不存在），第一個完整可用的當選；壞掉的會給出修復處方。實際的讀取和搜尋由 Agent 直接呼叫上游工具完成。 當前選型 場景 首選 備選 為什麼這麼選 讀網頁 Jina Reader — 免費，不需要 API Key 讀推特 twitter-cli OpenCLI 實測搜尋穩定；OpenCLI 走瀏覽器登入態兜底 Reddit OpenCLI （桌面） rdt-cli 匿名介面已被封、官方 API 審批制——只剩登入態路線 Facebook OpenCLI （桌面） — Graph API/Groups API 許可權收緊；瀏覽器登入態是當前最實用路徑 Instagram OpenCLI （桌面） 官方 Graph API（Business/Creator + 審批） instaloader 類路徑不穩定；OpenCLI 複用真實瀏覽器會話 YouTube 字幕 + 搜尋 yt-dlp — 154K Star，YouTube 仍是最佳（注意：不再用於 B站） B站 bili-cli OpenCLI ▸ 搜尋 API yt-dlp 被 B站風控 412 封死（2026-06 實測），bili-cli 無登入可搜可讀 搜全網 Exa via mcporter — AI 語義搜尋，MCP 接入免 Key GitHub gh CLI — 官方工具，認證後完整 API 能力 讀 RSS feedparser — Python 生態標準選擇 小紅書 OpenCLI （桌面） xiaohongshu-mcp （伺服器）▸ xhs-cli OpenCLI 只用使用者已有會話；其餘後端用 Cookie-Editor 手工匯出 LinkedIn mcp-server-linkedin Jina Reader MCP 服務，瀏覽器自動化 📌 這些都是「當前選型」，基於真機實測定期複核。某條路失效了我們換下一條—— agent-reach doctor 永遠告訴你現在走的是哪條。 安全性 Agent Reach 在設計上重視安全： 措施 說明 🔒 憑據本地儲存 Cookie、Token 只存在你本機 ~/.agent-reach/config.yaml ，檔案許可權 600（僅所有者可讀寫），不上傳不外傳 🛡️ 預設安全 agent-reach install 預設不修改系統；只有顯式 --system 才安裝外部工具和寫入配置 👀 完全開源 程式碼透明，隨時可審查。所有依賴工具也是開源專案 🔍 Dry Run agent-reach install --dry-run 預覽所有操作，不做任何改動 🧩 可插拔架構 不信任某個元件？換掉對應的 channel 檔案即可，不影響其他 🍪 Cookie 安全建議 ⚠️ 封號風險提醒： 使用 Cookie 登入的平臺（Twitter、小紅書等），通過指令碼/API 呼叫 存在被平臺檢測並封號的風險 。請務必使用 專用小號 ，不要用你的主賬號。 需要 Cookie 或登入態的平臺（Twitter、小紅書、Reddit、Facebook、Instagram 等）建議使用 專用小號 ，不要用主賬號。原因有二： 封號風險 — 平臺可能檢測到非正常瀏覽器的 API 呼叫行為，導致賬號被限制或封禁 安全風險 — Cookie 等同於完整登入許可權，用小號可以在憑據洩露時限制影響範圍 📦 安裝方式 方式 命令 適合場景 預設安全檢查 agent-reach install --env=auto 所有環境；只讀檢查並列出缺失項 顯式安裝系統依賴 agent-reach install --env=auto --system 你明確允許修改當前機器時 相容安全參數 agent-reach install --env=auto --safe 與預設行為相同 僅預覽 agent-reach install --env=auto --dry-run 先看看會做什麼 🗑️ 卸載 agent-reach uninstall 會清除： ~/.agent-reach/ （含所有 token/cookie）、各 Agent 的 skill 檔案、mcporter 中的 MCP 配置。 # 只預覽，不實際刪除 agent-reach uninstall --dry-run # 只刪 skill 檔案，保留 token 配置（重灌時用） agent-reach uninstall --keep-config 卸載 Python 包本身： pip uninstall agent-reach ⭐ 為什麼值得 Star 這個專案我自己每天在用，所以我會一直維護它。 有新需求或者大家提了想要的渠道，我會陸續加上 每個渠道我會盡量保證 能用、好用、免費 平臺改了反爬或者 API 變了，我會想辦法解決 為 Web 4.0 基建貢獻一份自己的力量。 Star 一下，下次需要的時候能找到。

title: tashfeenahmed/freellmapi
abstract: FreeLLMAPI 7.4 billion tokens per month.  34 free LLM providers. 635 free model endpoints. One OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Aggregate free tiers from dozens of providers, plus custom OpenAI-compatible chat, embedding, image, and audio endpoints, behind a single /v1 API. Keys are stored encrypted. A router picks the best available model for each request, falls over to the next provider when one is rate-limited, and tracks per-key usage so you stay under every free-tier cap. freellmapi.co · browse the full catalog: 474 model families, 635 free endpoints English · 簡體中文 · Русский Your router updates its own model catalog from a signed feed: new free models, quota changes, and compatibility fixes land without a git pull . Free installs get the monthly snapshot, so a model reaches them 30 days after it joins the live feed; premium routers get it the same day. Go live at freellmapi.co ($19/yr, cancel anytime). Contents Why this exists Supported providers Compatible CLIs & coding agents How it compares Features Quick start Desktop app Works with OpenAI-compatible clients Languages Premium (live catalog) Using the API Screenshots How it works FAQ Limitations Contributing Disclaimer Guides: Install & deploy · API reference · Clients & coding agents · Prompt compression · Architecture & internals · Documentation index · Contributor guide Why this exists Every serious AI lab now offers a free tier, a few million tokens a month, a few thousand requests a day. On its own each tier is a toy. Stacked together, they add up to roughly 7.4 billion tokens per month of working inference capacity, across 474 model families / 635 provider endpoints from small-and-fast to reasonably capable. The problem is that stacking them by hand is painful: thirty-four different SDKs, thirty-four different rate limits, thirty-four places a request can fail. FreeLLMAPI collapses that into one OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Point any OpenAI client library at your local server, and it routes transparently across whichever providers you've added keys for. And the free-tier landscape shifts weekly: providers launch models, retire them, and change quotas without notice. FreeLLMAPI tracks all of that for you. The router pulls a signed model catalog from freellmapi.co on its own, so your install keeps up without a git pull . See Premium (live catalog) for how fast it keeps up. Supported providers Google Groq Cerebras OpenCode Zen Mistral OpenRouter Cloudflare Cohere Z.ai (Zhipu) NVIDIA HuggingFace ModelScope Qwen3 · DeepSeek V4 · GLM-5 (needs Aliyun cn binding) … and 22 more free providers Plus a custom provider — point chat, embedding, image, or audio models at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM, a local Ollama, or a remote gateway) from the Keys page. The full, always-current list lives at freellmapi.co/models with per-model rate limits, context windows, and free-token budgets. Compatible CLIs & coding agents Claude Code Codex CLI Gemini CLI Cursor Cline Roo Code OpenCode Aider … plus Continue, Goose, Qwen Code, Kilo Code, Crush, Zed, JetBrains AI, DeepSeek Harness, MiMo Code, AtomCode, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Pi, Reasonix, ZCode and any OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini or Ollama client Most agents configure themselves with one command that reads your live catalog, backs up the existing config and merges into it: npx freellmapi setup-claude --url http://localhost:3001 --api-key < unified-key > All supported agents and their setup commands → · Per-tool recipes, MCP server and URL tokens → How it compares Based on public documentation, July 2026 — corrections welcome. Features Every OpenAI-style surface — /v1/chat/completions , /v1/responses (what Codex CLI needs), /v1/completions (editor ghost-text autocomplete), /v1/images/generations , /v1/videos/generations , /v1/audio/speech , /v1/audio/transcriptions , /v1/embeddings , and /v1/models — streaming and non-streaming, from the official SDKs or any OpenAI-compatible client. API reference → Anthropic Messages API — /v1/messages speaks Anthropic's wire format over the same router, so Claude Code and the official Anthropic SDKs run against your free pool. Details → Native Gemini + Ollama surfaces — Gemini CLI can use /v1beta ( generateContent , streaming, token counting, models), while opt-in Ollama emulation serves NDJSON chat/generate, tags, metadata, and embeddings for Zed, JetBrains, and other local-model clients. Fusion (multi-model synthesis) — request the virtual fusion model and the router fans your prompt out to a panel of diverse free models in parallel, then a judge model synthesizes one answer from the drafts. Details → Image, video & speech generation — /v1/images/generations , /v1/videos/generations , and /v1/audio/speech route across the providers that serve media models; images and speech also accept custom OpenAI-compatible media endpoints. Video jobs are normalized across synchronous and queued providers and return a completed MP4. Tool calling & structured outputs — OpenAI-style tools round-trip across providers (plain-text tool calls are rescued into real tool_calls ), plus response_format , seed , logprobs , penalties, and the rest of the sampling params passed through per provider. Smart routing, six strategies — live per-model speed/capability/reliability scores rank your chain; automatic fallover retries the next model on 429/5xx with cooldowns and key rotation. Routing in detail → Unified models & profiles — the same model on several providers collapses into one entry with strict in-group failover; named fallback-chain profiles (a coding chain, a vision chain) switch from the dashboard or per request via auto:<profile> , and custom chains can be renamed in place from the chain manager. Per-key rate tracking — RPM/RPD/TPM/TPD counters per (platform, model, key) that learn providers' reported ceilings, so routing always stays under every cap. Self-updating model catalog — the router syncs a signed catalog from freellmapi.co twice a day: new models, quota changes, and provider quirk fixes land automatically. Free installs track the monthly snapshot, which each model joins 30 days after it lands in the live feed; premium routers get it same-day. Premium → Sticky sessions & context handoff — conversations stay on one model for 30 minutes; an optional compact handoff note keeps the thread coherent when a mid-chat switch does happen. Details → Prompt compression (opt-in) — a shared, fail-open request pipeline can deduplicate prompts, filter tool output, compact repeated JSON, and trim stale context before cache lookup and routing. Details → Encrypted keys, one token out — provider keys are AES-256-GCM encrypted in SQLite and decrypted in-memory per request; your apps only ever see a single unified freellmapi-… bearer token. Admin dashboard & analytics — React UI to manage keys, reorder the chain, run a playground, and read p50/p95/TTFT analytics over 24h–90d windows; login-gated, dark/light themes, 60 languages . ChatGPT-ready MCP server & interactive docs — ChatGPT and other MCP clients can call FreeLLMAPI inference, list usable models, inspect provider health/usage/cache/routing metadata, and manage the routing strategy over /mcp ; a dependency-free OpenAPI viewer lives at /v1/docs . ChatGPT and coding agents → Ops niceties — opt-in response cache, encrypted DB backups, periodic key health checks, bulk key import/export, declarative startup config. Install & deploy → Runs anywhere Node 20+ runs — Windows, macOS, Linux servers, or a small ARM SBC (Raspberry Pi included). ~40 MB RSS at idle behind PM2 / systemd / whatever supervisor you prefer. The scope is deliberately narrow — see what's not supported yet . Quick start One-liner (Docker required — sets up ~/freellmapi , generates an encryption key, pulls the image, and starts the container): curl -fsSL https://freellmapi.co/install.sh | bash Prefer to read before you pipe to bash? The script is here . Re-running it is safe: your .

title: ItzCrazyKns/Vane
abstract: Vane 🔍 Vane is a privacy-focused AI answering engine that runs entirely on your own hardware. It combines knowledge from the vast internet with support for local LLMs (Ollama) and cloud providers (OpenAI, Claude, Groq), delivering accurate answers with cited sources while keeping your searches completely private. Want to know more about its architecture and how it works? You can read it here . ✨ Features 🤖 Support for all major AI providers - Use local LLMs through Ollama or connect to OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Groq, and more. Mix and match models based on your needs. ⚡ Smart search modes - Choose Speed Mode when you need quick answers, Balanced Mode for everyday searches, or Quality Mode for deep research. 🧭 Pick your sources - Search the web, discussions, or academic papers. More sources and integrations are in progress. 🧩 Widgets - Helpful UI cards that show up when relevant, like weather, calculations, stock prices, and other quick lookups. 🔍 Web search powered by SearxNG - Access multiple search engines while keeping your identity private. Support for Tavily and Exa coming soon for even better results. 📷 Image and video search - Find visual content alongside text results. Search isn't limited to just articles anymore. 📄 File uploads - Upload documents and ask questions about them. PDFs, text files, images - Vane understands them all. 🌐 Search specific domains - Limit your search to specific websites when you know where to look. Perfect for technical documentation or research papers. 💡 Smart suggestions - Get intelligent search suggestions as you type, helping you formulate better queries. 📚 Discover - Browse interesting articles and trending content throughout the day. Stay informed without even searching. 🕒 Search history - Every search is saved locally so you can revisit your discoveries anytime. Your research is never lost. ✨ More coming soon - We're actively developing new features based on community feedback. Join our Discord to help shape Vane's future! Sponsors Vane's development is powered by the generous support of our sponsors. Their contributions help keep this project free, open-source, and accessible to everyone. We'd like to thank the following partners for their generous support: Exa • The Perfect Web Search API for LLMs - web search, crawling, deep research, and answer APIs Installation There are mainly 2 ways of installing Vane - With Docker, Without Docker. Using Docker is highly recommended. Getting Started with Docker (Recommended) Vane can be easily run using Docker. Simply run the following command: docker run -d -p 3000:3000 -v vane-data:/home/vane/data --name vane itzcrazykns1337/vane:latest This will pull and start the Vane container with the bundled SearxNG search engine. Once running, open your browser and navigate to http://localhost:3000 . You can then configure your settings (API keys, models, etc.) directly in the setup screen. Note : The image includes both Vane and SearxNG, so no additional setup is required. The -v flags create persistent volumes for your data and uploaded files. Using Vane with Your Own SearxNG Instance If you already have SearxNG running, you can use the slim version of Vane: docker run -d -p 3000:3000 -e SEARXNG_API_URL=http://your-searxng-url:8080 -v vane-data:/home/vane/data --name vane itzcrazykns1337/vane:slim-latest Important : Make sure your SearxNG instance has: JSON format enabled in the settings Wolfram Alpha search engine enabled Replace http://your-searxng-url:8080 with your actual SearxNG URL. Then configure your AI provider settings in the setup screen at http://localhost:3000 . Advanced Setup (Building from Source) If you prefer to build from source or need more control: Ensure Docker is installed and running on your system. Clone the Vane repository: git clone https://github.com/ItzCrazyKns/Vane.git After cloning, navigate to the directory containing the project files. Build and run using Docker: docker build -t vane . docker run -d -p 3000:3000 -v vane-data:/home/vane/data --name vane vane Access Vane at http://localhost:3000 and configure your settings in the setup screen. Note : After the containers are built, you can start Vane directly from Docker without having to open a terminal. Non-Docker Installation Install SearXNG and allow JSON format in the SearXNG settings. Make sure Wolfram Alpha search engine is also enabled. Clone the repository: git clone https://github.com/ItzCrazyKns/Vane.git cd Vane Install dependencies: npm i Build the application: npm run build Start the application: npm run start Open your browser and navigate to http://localhost:3000 to complete the setup and configure your settings (API keys, models, SearxNG URL, etc.) in the setup screen. Note : Using Docker is recommended as it simplifies the setup process, especially for managing environment variables and dependencies. See the installation documentation for more information like updating, etc. Troubleshooting Local OpenAI-API-Compliant Servers If Vane tells you that you haven't configured any chat model providers, ensure that: Your server is running on 0.0.0.0 (not 127.0.0.1 ) and on the same port you put in the API URL. You have specified the correct model name loaded by your local LLM server. You have specified the correct API key, or if one is not defined, you have put something in the API key field and not left it empty. Ollama Connection Errors If you're encountering an Ollama connection error, it is likely due to the backend being unable to connect to Ollama's API. To fix this issue you can: Check your Ollama API URL: Ensure that the API URL is correctly set in the settings menu. Update API URL Based on OS: Windows: Use http://host.docker.internal:11434 Mac: Use http://host.docker.internal:11434 Linux: Use http://<private_ip_of_host>:11434 Adjust the port number if you're using a different one. Linux Users - Expose Ollama to Network: Inside /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service , you need to add Environment="OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434" . (Change the port number if you are using a different one.) Then reload the systemd manager configuration with systemctl daemon-reload , and restart Ollama by systemctl restart ollama . For more information see Ollama docs Ensure that the port (default is 11434) is not blocked by your firewall. Lemonade Connection Errors If you're encountering a Lemonade connection error, it is likely due to the backend being unable to connect to Lemonade's API. To fix this issue you can: Check your Lemonade API URL: Ensure that the API URL is correctly set in the settings menu. Update API URL Based on OS: Windows: Use http://host.docker.internal:8000 Mac: Use http://host.docker.internal:8000 Linux: Use http://<private_ip_of_host>:8000 Adjust the port number if you're using a different one. Ensure Lemonade Server is Running: Make sure your Lemonade server is running and accessible on the configured port (default is 8000). Verify that Lemonade is configured to accept connections from all interfaces ( 0.0.0.0 ), not just localhost ( 127.0.0.1 ). Ensure that the port (default is 8000) is not blocked by your firewall. Using as a Search Engine If you wish to use Vane as an alternative to traditional search engines like Google or Bing, or if you want to add a shortcut for quick access from your browser's search bar, follow these steps: Open your browser's settings. Navigate to the 'Search Engines' section. Add a new site search with the following URL: http://localhost:3000/?q=%s . Replace localhost with your IP address or domain name, and 3000 with the port number if Vane is not hosted locally. Click the add button. Now, you can use Vane directly from your browser's search bar. Using Vane's API Vane also provides an API for developers looking to integrate its powerful search engine into their own applications. You can run searches, use multiple models and get answers to your queries. For more details, check out the full documentation here .

title: trycua/cua
abstract:
Give AI agents computers they can use. Cua Spaces gives your agents full desktops on your Mac and on machines you own. This repository also holds Cua Driver for desktop automation, Lume for local VMs, CUA-S1 decision models and Cua Bench for evaluating computer-use agents. Get Cua Spaces Choose your path Cua Spaces: Install the app and run your first Space . Cua Driver: Operate Calculator and verify its result . Lume: Create a Tahoe VM and connect over SSH . Cua SDK and CLI: Install cua and create a local sandbox . CUA-S1: Explore small, specialized models for computer-use decisions . Cua Bench: Create and verify a simulated task . Bring your own agent and model, or explore CUA-S1 for specialized decisions. Cua provides the computer and automation tools. Computer-Use 2.0 describes an agent moving between code, APIs, and graphical interfaces within the same task. Cua Spaces Cua Spaces is a desktop app that gives your agents full desktops. Each desktop is a Space: a macOS VM built locally on your Mac, or a Linux or Omarchy image. Spaces run on your Mac, on other machines you own, and in your own cloud account (AWS, Google Cloud or Modal), and the app keeps them in your menu bar and notch. Teleport. Move a signed-in app, such as Chrome or Slack, into a Space and it opens there still signed in. Your sessions stay in the Cua Keyvault, encrypted on your Mac, and reach a Space only after you approve. Multiplayer. You and your agents work on the same desktop, each with your own cursor. Step in to make a choice, then hand the desktop back. Agent-ready images. Spaces images ship with cua-spacesd , so agents get processes, files, screenshots and input as soon as a Space starts. cua-spaces-demo.mp4 Install on macOS 26 or later curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/install.sh | sh On macOS the installer selects the Cua Spaces app by default and adds the cua CLI. You can also download the signed .dmg , or get the .pkg from the Cua Spaces 0.9.4 release . Spaces is free for individuals. Pro is $18 a month and Teams is $30 per seat a month, available now from 1 seat. See pricing . The app is source-available under FSL-1.1-MIT . Quickstart | Teleport an app | Share a Space | Host Spaces on a spare Mac (relay, Tailscale or SSH) | Your own cloud | App source Cua Driver Give your agent tools to inspect and operate native desktop apps and browsers on macOS, Windows, and Linux. Connect through the CLI, MCP, or typed SDKs. Background delivery lets agents work without moving your pointer or taking focus when the app and platform support it; see platform support for the boundaries. macOS / Linux /bin/bash -c " $( curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh ) " Windows (PowerShell) irm https: // cua.ai / driver / install.ps1 | iex Your first result: connect your agent, ask it to compute 6 × 7 in Calculator, and have it verify that the app displays 42. The tutorial covers platform setup, permissions, and agent connection. Drive your first app | Installation | CLI Reference Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, or another agent? Find your integration . Source documentation and architecture notes live in libs/cua-driver/README.md . See Cua Driver in action Two Cua Driver sessions select cells in LibreOffice Calc and objects in Inkscape on an Omarchy desktop while a terminal stays in the foreground. Watch the 50-second demo. recording.mp4 Lume Create and manage local macOS and Linux VMs on Apple Silicon using Apple's Virtualization.Framework. /bin/bash -c " $( curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/lume/install.sh ) " Your first result: create a vanilla macOS Tahoe VM from an Apple restore image, start it, and connect over SSH. The tutorial uses the Lume CLI directly and explains the unattended setup defaults. Create your first Lume VM | Installation | CLI reference Cua SDK and CLI One SDK and one cua command for local VMs and containers, and for any machine that runs cua-spacesd . macOS / Linux curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/install.sh | sh Windows (PowerShell) irm https: // cua.ai / install.ps1 | iex In a terminal the script first says what Cua Spaces is. The command-line tools (the cua program) are always installed; you choose whether to add the Cua Spaces app (on by default) and Cua Driver, which lets AI agents use your apps while you keep working (off by default). It then runs cua auth login , which signs you in and offers to set up your AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others). The app asks on its first run whether your other devices may use this computer. Add Cua Driver with sh -s -- --select cua-driver , or skip the choice with --only cua-driver . See the installer options . cua sb create ubuntu --name dev # a gVisor container, set up on first use cua sb exec dev uname -a
cua sb screenshot dev
cua sb rm dev The same sandbox from Python: from cua_sandbox import Image , Sandbox async with Sandbox . ephemeral ( Image . linux (), local = True ) as sb : print (( await sb . shell . run ( "uname -a" )). stdout ) SDK: the same API in Python ( pip install cua ), TypeScript ( @trycua/cua ) and Rust ( cua-sdk ), running embedded in your process or through a shared cua daemon . Swift and Kotlin bindings are not yet released. Sandboxes need no agent inside. Readiness comes from the runtime and optional port probes. Images that ship cua-spacesd (port 3211) add processes, files, screenshots, input through cua-driver, and low-latency video and audio streaming. There is no agent layer in the SDK either: drive sandboxes from your own harness ( guide ). Your own machines. cua host setup makes this machine reachable through the cua.ai relay with no port forwarding. SDK README | Quickstart | CLI reference | Sandbox SDK reference CUA-S1 CUA-S1 is our family of small, specialized System 1 models for computer use. We use "System 1" as an engineering analogy for fast, bounded decisions, such as choosing which value belongs in a field or whether to leave an element alone. It is not a strict classification of model architectures or a replacement for a general-purpose agent's planning and reasoning. The first research profile focuses on forms: scoring decisions from structured interface elements and document values rather than generating a response token by token. Application code orders the actions, and the optional Cua Driver integration handles execution with explicit action boundaries. The project includes Python model code, synthetic-data generation, training, and evaluation. The GitHub component is an early, source-only research release; model weights are hosted separately on Hugging Face. The source is MIT-licensed. Check each model and dataset card for its scope, limitations, and artifact-specific license. Explore CUA-S1 | Model card | Safety and deployment guidance CUA-S1-FORMS on Hugging Face: Model weights | Dataset Cua Bench Build computer-use tasks, evaluate agents, and export trajectories for training. Start with a simulated task that requires no VM, Docker, or model API key. With Python 3.12 or 3.13 and uv installed: uv tool install ' cua-bench[browser] ' uv tool run --from ' cua-bench[browser] ' playwright install chromium Your first result: create a small task, run its reference solution, and verify that its evaluator reports a reward of 1.0 . Then try the same task yourself. Build your first task | What is Cua-Bench?

title: openai/codex
abstract: Codex CLI is a coding agent from OpenAI that runs locally on your computer. If you want Codex in your code editor (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf), install in your IDE. If you want the desktop app experience, run codex app or visit the Codex App page . If you are looking for the cloud-based agent from OpenAI, Codex Web , go to chatgpt.com/codex . Quickstart Installing and running Codex CLI Run the following on Mac or Linux to install Codex CLI: curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh Run the following on Windows to install Codex CLI: powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c " irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex " The standalone installers download from https://releases.openai.com/codex by default and fall back to GitHub Releases if a metadata or asset download is unavailable. To force GitHub Releases, set CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM to false ( 0 and no are also accepted): curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM=false sh $ env: CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM = ' false ' ; irm https: // chatgpt.com / codex / install.ps1 | iex Codex CLI can also be installed via the following package managers: # Install using npm npm install -g @openai/codex # Install using Homebrew brew install --cask codex Then simply run codex to get started. You can also go to the latest GitHub Release and download the appropriate binary for your platform. Each GitHub Release contains many executables, but in practice, you likely want one of these: macOS Apple Silicon/arm64: codex-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz x86_64 (older Mac hardware): codex-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz Linux x86_64: codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz arm64: codex-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz Each archive contains a single entry with the platform baked into the name (e.g., codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl ), so you likely want to rename it to codex after extracting it. Using Codex with your ChatGPT plan Run codex and select Sign in with ChatGPT . We recommend signing into your ChatGPT account to use Codex as part of your Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, or Enterprise plan. Learn more about what's included in your ChatGPT plan . You can also use Codex with an API key, but this requires additional setup . Docs Codex Documentation Contributing Installing & building Open source fund This repository is licensed under the Apache-2.0 License .

title: Show HN: I told people I'm a convicted felon after 20 years of hiding it
abstract: Hi there. I was engineer number 3 at Eventbrite and founding engineer at Reforge. I've created a dozen or so startups myself and have worked in many others, like Instacart. All this time, no one knew that I was a convicted felon. It wasn't exactly a topic that came up, but it was certainly something that I never brought up. When you're a convicted felon, people look at you as if you are tainted. I was unable to rent apartments in San Francisco. I was unable to get a job directly after being released from prison. It's funny because when you owe the state $17,000 in restitution and you can't get a job, people become extremely desperate. And that desperation can easily put you right back into prison. So I went from homeless person at age 19 to 7-figures about 10 years later. I retired at age 38. What I'm doing now is writing an autobiography. The main theme of it is hope. And I want to make sure that people know about it. They don't necessarily have to be interested in it, but if people know about what it's like sleeping in a car believing that one day you will travel the world and then actually doing it, then I think I've accomplished my task in writing this book. If you're interested, please let me know.
